reels.summary: The official Guns N' Roses account announces the band's 2026 World Tour, with tickets on sale Friday, December 5th at 10am local time.

reels.title: Why Pure Vector Search Fails in Production RAG
reels.summary: Banias (@baniascodes) argues pure vector search is not enough for production RAG and lays out the fix: (1) hybrid search is mandatory — combine BM25 keyword search with vector search, since embeddings are great for concepts ("dog" ~ "puppy") but terrible for exact matches like product IDs or specific legal clauses; (2) use Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) rather than averaging scores to normalize the keyword and vector rankings; (3) re-ranking is "the secret sauce" — retrieve 50 documents instead of 5, then pass them through a cross-encoder like BGE-Reranker to sort by true relevance before the LLM; (4) metadata filtering — don't search the whole database, pre-filter by year, category, or source before vector search runs.

reels.title: visualrambling.space: Data as Art
reels.summary: A name.com (@namedotcom) reel tours visualrambling.space, a site that blends data and design: Ramudita narrates a screen recording showcasing its articles and data visualizations, highlighting pieces on techniques like dithering alongside popular topics such as Christopher Nolan movie rankings and K-pop popularity across countries. The pitch is "data, but make it art" — the perfect blend of data and design.

reels.title: The 7 Luxury Flatware Sets Worth Buying
reels.summary: Caleb Ulffers (@calebulf) presents the seven luxury flatware sets he would buy right now, combining live presentation with professional product photography covering each set's design, material, origin, and price. Brands featured include @theluxuryartmepra, @christofle, @schiavon_silverware, @pottflatware, @ercuis, and @alain_saint_joanis — appreciating the beauty and craftsmanship even where the price is out of reach. Comment "Flatware" to get a link.

reels.title: Perfect Late City Night Vibes: Jazz & City Pop Mix
reels.summary: Dorian (@dorianmualem) shares a late-night city vibes vinyl mix blending city pop, jazz fusion, and Japanese jazz — hashtags point to Yussef Dayes, Tom Misch, and Daft Punk's "Something About Us." A short, atmospheric late-night-drive music reel.

reels.title: Underrated or Overrated?
reels.summary: Luke Damant (@lukedamant) rates travel destinations around the world as overrated, underrated, or perfectly rated in a comedic, opinionated studio-mic review, backing each rating with his own travel experiences and reasons. Lighthearted take on popular tourist spots.

reels.title: The Hyte X50 Cherry Red PC Case
reels.summary: Brittany Marie (@techtesseract) reviews the HYTE X50 PC case in Cherry Red (shown anime-decorated): unique curves and vibrant color with early-2000s tech nostalgia, PSU mounted at the top, an easily removable curved glass panel, excellent cable management where "every inch looks intentional," and room for up to 10 fans for cooling performance. It comes in green, purple, and pink with matching fans, and she includes a matching cherry candle as a cute touch (not included with the case). She notes the X50 follows the trend the Y70 started.

reels.title: When Chaos Is Your Middle Name: Oakley the Horse
reels.summary: Myhorsewillow (@myhorsewillow) shares a chaotic, affectionate play session with Oakley the horse in a grassy field. After a polite, calm ride up and down hills, she takes the halter off and lets him run loose to follow her home — something they've done since he was six months old: they run one direction, she turns and runs the other, and he spins and chases after her. She loves it and says she can read his every intention because they've been together since the moment he was born (her sister, notably, does not enjoy these walks). The caption jokes about the saddle flaps looking like wings at the start of the video.

reels.title: Top-3 Brisket at Heavy's Smokehouse (San Diego)
reels.summary: Camille (@sandiegofoodgems) reviews Heavy's Smokehouse, the Texas-style barbecue food truck in San Ysidro run by owner Heavy — "your favorite heavy metal barbecue guy." She calls his brisket a definite top-3-all-time: perfectly seasoned, flavor retained rather than drowned out by fat, "absolute FIRE." The ribs are smoky and flavorful (she was shocked she could actually taste the smoke, in the best way), the maple baked beans balance sweet and savory, and the gouda mac and cheese gets a dramatic cheese pull. Tried at @sdmetalswapmeet, with a pro tip that the BBQ pairs perfectly with a cold one.

reels.title: 28 PTO Days = 66 Days of Freedom in 2026
reels.summary: Bergit | Travel (@viabergit) shares a PTO-maximization guide for 2026 as a static airplane-wing-at-sunset graphic: by strategically placing days off around holidays, 28 PTO days become 66 days of freedom. A save-worthy vacation-planning cheat sheet for the work-life-balance crowd.

reels.title: Mom's Special Chicken Shorba (Soup Season)
reels.summary: Fathima Yusuf (Shadiya, @shadi_faleel) kicks off her "soup season" series with Mom's Special Chicken Shorba — a spicy chicken-and-coriander soup. The caption gives the full ingredient list: blend onion, ginger, garlic, cumin seeds, black pepper, coriander, and water; then temper in ghee with urad daal, cumin seeds, cloves, cardamoms, curry leaves, and onion, adding salt, hot water, coriander/turmeric/cumin powders, crushed coriander stems, julienned ginger, and fresh coriander. Served with toasted bread or a bowl of rice — a hearty winter warmer for chilly weather.

reels.title: Shadowbrook: A Top-20 Romantic Restaurant in Capitola
reels.summary: Asya Olson (@asyatravels) vlogs Shadowbrook Restaurant at 1750 Wharf Rd, Capitola, CA — named one of the Top 20 Most Romantic Restaurants in the World. Shadowbrook is older than the city of Capitola itself; you reach it by hillside cable car or garden-path stairs, and inside are seven unique dining rooms, one with a giant cypress tree growing through it, set among lush gardens with river views. And yes, the food is amazing too.

reels.title: The Weighted Cow for Better Sleep & Calm
reels.summary: A sponsored ad from Pulse of Potential (@pulseofpotential) for The Weighted Cow — a weighted plush promising the cozy pressure your body craves to help you unwind faster, fall asleep easier, and soothe nighttime anxiety naturally, as part of a nighttime routine. The caption pushes a "today only" promo of 30% off plus 2 free gifts, framing it as self-care.

reels.title: Fly a Real Boeing 737 Simulator in LA
reels.summary: LA EATS (@losangeles_eats) spotlights WeFly (@weflyaero) in Los Angeles, where you can fly a REAL Boeing 737 or Airbus simulator with a real pilot teaching you — no experience required. You choose your flight plan (takeoff, route, landing), weather, and time of day to watch sunsets or feel turbulence; kids 10+ can fly, and the instructor can take over anytime. Located at 1 W Mountain St, Unit 9, Pasadena, CA 91103 — billed as the only place in LA with this experience and the only Airbus simulator in California.

reels.title: Replay Terminal Commands Like a Movie
reels.summary: NetworkChuck demos asciinema, a command-line tool that records terminal sessions into small text-based files you can replay like a movie — he records his own session, saves it locally, and plays it back. He also shows asciinema_agg, a companion tool that converts those recordings into animated GIFs. Enthusiastic, playful walkthrough.

reels.title: Vert: Convert Files 100% Locally in Your Browser
reels.summary: GitHub's (@github) reel promotes VERT, an open-source file-conversion tool that converts files 100% locally in your browser using WebAssembly — no uploading sensitive files to random websites. Jenna Marbles demos its extensive format support and privacy focus via a screen recording of the GitHub repo and web UI, closing with a humorous exaggerated face of surprise.

reels.title: 5 Interesting Open Source Projects This Week
reels.summary: Software developer Lewis Menelaws (@lewismenelaws) rounds up five open-source projects he found interesting this week: Dioxus (a cross-platform UI framework), Servo (a lightweight browser engine), DNS Blocklists (a privacy-focused tool), Pocketbase (a real-time backend), and Bettafish (an AI-powered public opinion analyzer). Conversational, humorous tech review with screen recordings — "Would you use any of these?"

reels.title: Fun Websites to Cure Your Boredom
reels.summary: Matty McTech (@setupspawn) demos three fun websites to cure boredom, with step-by-step narration synced to screen recordings: Geo-FS, a browser-based flight simulator where you pick an aircraft and fly anywhere; My Retro TV, for virtually browsing 1990s TV channels complete with cartoons and commercials; and McStumble, which serves up random websites for discovery based on categories you define.

reels.title: 5 No-Skip Albums Perfect for Hosting
reels.summary: Agustina Arcolia (@agusarcolia) recommends five no-skip albums that are perfect for hosting guests at home — each showcased with its artwork, title, artist, genre, and a snippet of the music. Jazz and bossa-nova leaning; the full picks live in her "Agus Arcolia" Spotify playlist (link in bio).

reels.title: An Underrated 2013 Bollywood Dark Comedy Gem
reels.summary: Siddhant Yadav (@siddhantyadavv) recommends the 2013 Bollywood dark comedy 'Ghanchakkar' as a criminally underrated, deliciously dark gem "wayyy ahead of its time." The plot: bank robber Sanjay loses his memory in an accident and forgets both his accomplices and the stolen money — is he truly amnesiac, or lying to keep the cash? He praises the performances of Emraan Hashmi and Vidya Balan, calls it one of his all-time favorites, and urges viewers not to sleep on it; it's available to watch on YouTube.

reels.title: The Perfect California Detour Destination
reels.summary: A Wild Times Podcast (@wildtimespod) sponsored road trip by Toyota Trucks: a scenic NorCal drive starting in San Francisco (drive or rent a Toyota truck), with a first stop at Tomales Bay for fresh oysters at Hog Island Oyster Company overlooking the bay, then up Highway 1 past redwoods, coastal bluffs, and hills of grazing sheep, a detour to the "secret" town of Duncan Mills ("Jurassic Park"-like with giant ferns and redwoods), and on to Gualala — home of a "live termite round" attraction — with a stay at the Sea Ranch Inn billed as a "perfect vacation." Tagged #ad and #ToyotaPartner.

reels.title: Dzükou Valley: India's Hidden Valley
reels.summary: Pranav Selot (@_travelwithsel_) hikes alone through Dzükou Valley in Nagaland, joking that he and his sister are the only people in the vast valley: rolling green hills and meadows, sitting on a large carved rock taking in the view, drinking from a clear river. He notes 70% of the valley falls in Manipur — where he started, right by the Manipur border — and that most Indians don't even know the place exists, which he calls a shame but also a blessing lest it be ruined like other tourist spots.

reels.title: Testing the Perfect Egg Pan (Strata Cookware)
reels.summary: Michael Tchao (@michaeltchao) tests a pan gifted by Strata Cookware in his hunt for the perfect egg pan: an 8" multi-material pan (stainless steel, aluminum core, carbon steel) that he seasons and then uses to cook an omelet at low heat — successfully. What he likes: it's lightweight (easy to slide eggs onto the plate, unlike heavy cast iron), the aluminum core heats faster and more consistently than straight carbon steel, the surface is naturally non-stick and non-toxic, and it's warp-resistant for smooth-top cooking. He'll be testing it all year, and Strata set up code "Tchao10" for 10% off.

reels.title: Top 5 Fastest TTK Loadouts in Battlefield 6
reels.summary: Chuck (@chuckthecg) presents his top five fastest TTK (time-to-kill) loadouts in Battlefield 6 in a split-screen reel with gameplay: the DRS-IAR for all-range versatility, the "slept on" UMG 40 SMG for its negligible recoil, the SG 553-R carbine (worthwhile despite recoil), his favorite the Cord AR — "an absolute menace" and the overall best AR — and the B-36A4 AR for balanced moderate fire rate and recoil control.

reels.title: Top 5 Meta Loadouts in Battlefield 6
reels.summary: Chuck (@chuckthecg) runs down his top five meta loadouts in Battlefield 6, commentating over first-person gameplay with his favorite weapon loadouts and personal experience with each. Straightforward, enthusiastic meta guide for BF6 players.

reels.title: Fable's Japanese Glassware Review
reels.summary: Michael Tchao (@michaeltchao) reviews Fable's (@fablehome) Japanese glassware: stacking glasses made by Japan's top glassmaker, Toyo-Sasaki, that are super thin, nice to drink from, and significantly stronger than traditional glass — with stackable, space-saving storage demonstrated in his kitchen. Not an ad, just a product he loves.

reels.title: Ship It: Perfect Code Means Nothing If Nobody Wants It
reels.summary: Angus the Nontechnical (@angus.sewell) delivers a founder-mindset take on vibe-coding culture: "Dude just ship the thing — perfect code means nothing if nobody wants it." The argument is to prioritize shipping a product and validating it with real users over spending months on perfect architecture, wrapped in a rapid-fire showcase of 11 software tools for AI coding, UI components, authentication, databases, payments, emails, storage, analytics, deployment, and workflows.

reels.title: Instant AI Website Design: Opportunity or Threat?
reels.summary: Andres Franco (@theinsiders_club) covers Pomelli, a new Google Labs AI tool for instant website/marketing design (opened with a gag of Sundar Pichai pressing a "Google" button followed by an explosion): type in a website and instantly get infographics generated from your company's "Business DNA." His take is split — don't freak out, see the money-making opportunity: generate designs under different accounts, then cold-outreach companies showing the results as a numbers-game side hustle worth realistically $1–2k/month. But long-term, he argues designers should worry: if one designer with this tool ships 10x more creatives, the design job market shrinks.

reels.title: The Perfect Cheese on Toast
reels.summary: Adam Lind (@adam.floatinghome) shares his elevated cheese-on-toast recipe: cheddar cheese, 1 egg, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard, and garlic paste, combined (adjusting mustard and Worcestershire to taste), spread on bread, and baked. He tastes it at the end, surprised and delighted at how good it is.

reels.title: Use NotebookLM for Vibe-Coding Prompt Creation
reels.summary: James Goldbach (@agentic.james) lays out a vibe-coding workflow using Google's NotebookLM for prompt creation: use NotebookLM's source-finding to gather relevant documentation at the start of a project, combine it with insights from GitHub repos (found via another LLM and processed with GitInjest) that implement the features you want, and synthesize everything into a context-dense system prompt for your coding agent — significantly improving the agent's efficiency and effectiveness.

reels.title: BF6 Aim Glitch Fix & Best Controller Settings
reels.summary: THE Patman (@thepatmanstudios) — host Synapse — identifies an aim glitch in Battlefield 6 that makes the crosshair slip off targets for both mouse/keyboard and controller players, then gives a step-by-step fix in the controller settings menu: update Aim Zoom Transition Timing, Infantry Uniform Aiming, Left/Right Acceleration, and Aim Assist Slowdown for the stickiest aim and max aim assist. Split-screen format demonstrating smooth aiming and successful kills with the fix applied.

reels.title: Advanced HUD Settings for Battlefield 6
reels.summary: THE Patman (@thepatmanstudios) covers the advanced HUD settings you need in Battlefield 6 — customizing your mini-map, killfeed, and awareness. A quick settings guide reel.

reels.summary: Carissa (@minibarnmarket) gives the practical details for the Mini Barn Market 24/7 honor-system farm stand: prices are marked on items, and payment is accepted via cash, card, Venmo, Zelle, and Apple Pay. reels.creator_name: Carissa | 24/7 Honor System Farmstand & Farm Resorts

reels.title: Unlimited Dim Sum for $34.99 at China Max (San Diego)
reels.summary: Cindy Wang (@cinfullyfoodie) spotlights all-you-can-eat dim sum at China Max in San Diego (@chinamaxsandiego): $34.99 on weekdays, $37.99 on weekends. The refreshed menu has over 45 items — juicy xiao long bao, har gow, shumai, pan-fried xiao long bao, wagyu dumplings, spicy wontons, cold appetizers, noodles, dishes, fluffy desserts, buns, and fruit tea — all super fresh because you can watch the aunties making the dumplings from scratch. "You win sum, you dim sum."

reels.title: Emraan Hashmi's 3 Truly Underrated Masterpieces
reels.summary: The Shiro Bro (@theshirobro), commentator Nakul Mehta, picks three truly underrated Emraan Hashmi masterpieces in a split-screen film analysis with clips: 'Shanghai' (2012), 'Raja Natwarlal' (2014), and 'Cheat India' (2019) — giving a brief synopsis of each film's plot and themes in an informative, analytical tone.

reels.title: Darna Mana Hai (2003): Bollywood's Underrated Horror Anthology
reels.summary: Siddhant Yadav (@siddhantyadavv) champions 'Darna Mana Hai' (2003) as one of early-2000s Bollywood's most underrated gems: a horror anthology that dared to trust storytelling over loud music and cheap scares, built around a group of people whose scary stories play out as short films. Highlights include the 'No Smoking' segment starring Saif Ali Khan and Boman Irani and a story with Nana Patekar and Vivek Oberoi, with Shilpa Shetty also in the cast — proof that Indian cinema once respected horror as a space for creativity. It flopped at the box office, so audiences never got the anthology universe it deserved, and he invites viewers to share their favorite stories from it and its sequel 'Darna Zaroori Hai' in the comments.

reels.title: Leonhard Euler Math Meme
reels.summary: Infinite Dimensional (@dimensionless_memes) posts a satirical intellectual meme: text overlay reads "Mathematicians when you say '2+2=4' without first defining the Peano-Dedekind axioms and ontological legitimacy of numbers as an equivalence class of cardinalities under bijective mappings," paired with a black-and-white photo of Bertrand Russell. The caption runs with the bit — a Leonhard Euler bio (graph theory and topology founder, analytic number theory, complex analysis, infinitesimal calculus), a silly formula "f(x) = x + 's', x ∈ W," and a thank-you to @everythingquant.

reels.title: Indian Groom Outfits with Prices (kalpraag)
reels.summary: Chahat Chaudhary (@chahatchaudhary_) lists approximate INR prices for 17 Indian groom outfits from brand @kalpraag, ranging from ₹11,744 (worn by @yoyohoneysingh) up to ₹94,999 — most landing between ₹16,400 and ₹48,663, including looks worn by @aparshakti_khurana (₹21,510) and @kkundrra (₹19,509), plus pink and maroon options. She notes viewers should verify prices with the brand directly since discrepancies happen.

reels.title: Making 210 Momos After Work
reels.summary: Gaurav (@__gauravraii) documents an after-work cooking marathon: he made 210 momos plus some starters in just three hours — by himself — for a party of 13. A time-lapse montage covers making the filling, cooking a starter, and plating, ending with a proud showcase of the finished spread.

reels.title: Pattern & Wallpaper Search Terms That Make Styling Easier
reels.summary: Brynn Smith-Jenkins (@brynnsmithjenkins) teaches the specific names and search terms for common patterns and wallpapers, showing each pattern's name alongside a visual example in split-screen — arguing that knowing the exact terms (plaids, stripes, and more) makes styling your life much easier. She apologizes in advance for any mispronunciations: "I'm just a Texas gal who loves patterns and design from all over the world."

reels.title: 5-Minute Black Pepper Chicken
reels.summary: Mitchell (@i.am.never.full) makes black pepper chicken in five minutes as part of his 'After 9 to 5' series — joking that the only things stopping him from ordering Uber Eats are the meal he's about to cook and his bank account. The reel covers marinating the chicken, preparing the sauce, and cooking the final dish served over rice and eaten with satisfaction. Full recipe goes to your inbox if you comment "Recipe," or at iamneverfull.com/black-pepper-chicken.

reels.title: Crucial BF6 Settings for Aim & Movement (PS5/Xbox/PC)
reels.summary: THE Patman (@thepatmanstudios) walks through the crucial Battlefield 6 settings for aim and movement on PS5, Xbox, and PC in a picture-in-picture tutorial: specific recommendations across the Aim, Movement, Other, and Controller Tuning sections, with on-screen text highlighting key settings and values — all aimed at precise aim and smooth movement to "dominate the battlefield."

reels.title: The Darjeeling Limited (2007): A Wes Anderson Journey
reels.summary: obnoir (@obscnoir) pens an appreciation of Wes Anderson's The Darjeeling Limited (2007): three estranged brothers reunite for a train journey across India, each carrying grief and unspoken regrets, their pasts tangling with present tensions as they search for connection and meaning. Encounters with strangers and unexpected adventures challenge their assumptions about family and forgiveness, and the journey becomes a mosaic of humor, discomfort, and quiet reflection — a bittersweet beauty blending melancholy with whimsy, exploring reconciliation and self-discovery against a rich, colorful backdrop.

reels.title: Bobby Deol's Top 3 Suspense Thrillers
reels.summary: Filmein aur Fasaadh | Vivek Khar (@filmein_aur_fasaadh) ranks Bobby Deol's top three suspense thrillers with the best plot twists — 'Gupt,' 'Ajnabee,' and 'Humraaz,' all directed by Abbas-Mustan — in a split-screen reel with the narrator up top and posters/clips below. He teases a bonus 2007 film at the end and asks viewers to guess its name in the comments.

reels.title: How Thinking Machines Changed Model Training
reels.summary: Reshad (@remoteree) reports that Thinking Machines just changed the model-training game: its Tinker API lets indie hackers fine-tune massive language models — a task previously limited to large corporations — using low-rank adapters so multiple users share GPU resources on a single frozen base model, making it incredibly cost-effective. His pitch: "anybody can do what the big tech corporations are doing right now," and it's time for a broad audience to get into machine learning. Opens with a humorous apology to Mira Murati.

reels.title: Perfect Suji Halwa (No-Fail Recipe)
reels.summary: Bharat Wadhwa (@bharatzkitchen) shares his no-fail suji halwa recipe ("Ab mere Halwe ka cake nahi banega"): 1/2 cup barik suji, 1/2 cup desi ghee, 1/2 cup sugar, 1.5 cups water, 3 elaichi, 4 tbsp milk, 1 tbsp besan, and 4–5 kesar strands. Method: sauté dry fruits in ghee, toast the semolina with a spoonful of gram flour (besan) for a soft texture, steam with water, add sugar, and finish with ghee and cardamom powder — served creatively in crispy pastry shells. Framed as Navratri/Durga Puja prasad for Ashtami/Navami/Kanjak.

reels.title: You Got the Dunning-Kruger Effect
reels.summary: Nate Nate (@neurodivergent__nate) delivers a passionate monologue arguing that anyone claiming expertise about a specific demographic — say, pregnant women or autistic children — should be able to answer fundamental questions about research methodology: p-values, statistical significance, IRBs, statistical models, sampling methods, study designs, and quantitative vs. qualitative research. His point: true expertise means actively analyzing data, justifying methods, interpreting findings, and disseminating them coherently — not just consuming research. Caption: "Y'all got the Dunning-Kruger effect."

reels.title: Vanilla Bean Cold Brew with Creamy Cold Foam
reels.summary: Matt (@created2coffee) makes a vanilla bean cold brew with creamy cold foam that "feels like dessert in a cup": cold foam of 3 tbsp heavy whipping cream, 2 tbsp milk, and 1 tbsp powdered sugar frothed until silky smooth, layered over ice and cold brew with Amoretti Vanilla Bean Bourbon syrup. Stir, sip, and enjoy — "who needs milkshakes when your cold brew tastes THIS good?"

reels.title: Relatable Text Memes
reels.summary: Meme page @teddy.talks_shit shares a relatable text-meme reel built around a satirical street-art poster on a pole: a deadpan bit that elevates vomiting to a "true Zen state" and criticizes the modern habit of using phones while defecating, landing on the punchline "Then God has truly lost." Ironic, crude social commentary with a melancholic intro; the caption just says "Follow for more."

reels.title: The Mongol Rally: 15,000 km in a Tiny Hatchback
reels.summary: Not Standard Issue (@not_standard_issue) pitches the Mongol Rally: a 15,000 km road trip in a tiny hatchback from Prague to Mongolia, where "to enter you have to have a bad car, a lack of self preservation, and 6 weeks off work." The £895 team entry fee gets you start and finish line events, a support network of fellow drivers, and rally livery (T-shirts and stickers). To sign up, go to the Adventurists website and "enter a team" — ideally with reliable friends or strangers, a witty team name, and a car idea. "Do your own Top Gear special."

reels.title: Lachha Pyaz (Reel 159/200)
reels.summary: Masterr_of_cooking_ (@masterr_of_cooking_), reel 159/200, gives a step-by-step for two classic Indian sides: masala (lachha) pyaz — soak sliced onions in ice water to mellow them, then toss with chaat masala, Kashmiri chili powder, black salt, mustard oil, lemon juice, and fresh coriander; and green chutney — blend coriander leaves, mint leaves, green chilies, hing, salt, and ice. Both are presented with flatbread as a complete meal.

reels.title: Grief
reels.summary: Streamer Chupumballs (@chupumballs) reacts — visibly moved and contemplative — to a cinematic piece set in a video game environment, where a character by a fireplace listens to a narrator's deeply personal story about grief. The narrator argues grief cannot be "dealt with" but must be carried as a testament to the love you had for the person lost; he recounts the deaths of his father and his best friend, and closes with hope: the love remains, and that is enough to keep living.

reels.title: Top-Rated Burrito Spots in San Diego (per Beli)
reels.summary: Beli - Restaurant Lists (@beli_eats) ranks the top-rated burrito spots in San Diego based on 75 million Beli ratings: Mike's Taco Club (@mikestacoclub), Ortiz's Taco Shop (@ortizstacoshop), and La Perla 3 (@laperlasandiego) — with La Perla #3 the highest-rated at 9.5. Appetizing close-ups, text-overlay rankings, and exterior shots, plus an invitation to comment on what should have made the list.

reels.title: ChatGPT 'God Mode' (Comment for Link)
reels.summary: Kushank Aggarwal (@digitalsamaritan) demos Prompt Genie, billed as "unlocking ChatGPT GOD mode": type a task, select a project context, and the tool generates a highly structured "super prompt" to improve AI output, with a free Chrome extension shown working inside another AI interface. Comment "super" for the link.

reels.title: One of the Greatest YouTube Videos Ever Made
reels.summary: Ludwig Ahgren (@ludwigahgren) gives a passionate, hyperbolic endorsement of the YouTube video "1000 Players Simulate Civilization: Rich & Poor," calling it the greatest YouTube video of all time — significant as "the entire history of the world" — and explicitly urging his audience to watch it, dismissing any notion that it's just a meme or a joke. "This is no joke one of the greatest YouTube videos ever made — I truly believe this with my whole damn heart."

reels.title: AYCE Mediterranean Buffet in Cerritos — Dimassi's
reels.summary: Greg Simms revisits Dimassi's Mediterranean Buffet at 12727 Towne Center in Cerritos, impressed by the buffet's size, variety, and price: $20 for lunch, $25/$28 for dinners and weekends (when lamb shanks are served). He calls it a one-of-a-kind, family-run SoCal spot built on mom's recipes and her love and attention in the kitchen.

reels.title: Hyperwrite AI: Operate Your Browser With a Text Prompt
reels.summary: Sagar Amruth demos HyperWrite AI, an AI assistant that operates your web browser from a text prompt. The screen recording shows it searching for information, sending an email, and posting on Twitter, with his real-time narration walking through each task. An informative, tutorial-style overview of the browser agent's capabilities.

reels.title: A Bronx Tale — Movie Moment
reels.summary: Bryce Vaughn, 'Da Narrator,' gives a passionate fan review of Robert De Niro's 1993 film A Bronx Tale, calling it his favorite mafia movie. He recounts the coming-of-age story of a Bronx boy torn between his honest bus-driver father and the local mobster Sonny, who becomes a father figure, and praises the film's narrative and soundtrack over clips set in 1960s New York City.

reels.title: Highway Gomantak, Bandra — Mini Food Vlog
reels.summary: Aavi Vadekar's mini vlog visits Highway Gomantak, a popular Malvani restaurant in Bandra East, Mumbai (Gandi Nagar, Kalanagar), narrated with the viral 'Big Bull' audio meme from the Indian reality show for a humorous trend-participation effect. The reel celebrates the Malvani food experience as an 'after Shravan party' suggestion — shareable, lighthearted food content shot by @dhanraj.96.

reels.title: Two Must-Have Anatomy Books for Artists
reels.summary: Artist Shubham Pathak recommends two must-have anatomy books by Aditya Chari: 'Portrait Techniques,' for its shading methods, and 'Figure Study Made Easy,' which he calls a gem for its clear information and special section on perspective. Filmed in his purple-lit studio, he closes by saying books are a great source of knowledge.

reels.title: Chicken Shawarma Wrap
reels.summary: Marshmello, in his trademark helmet, makes a chicken shawarma wrap: chicken marinated in spices and sauces, stacked on a vertical rotisserie, oven-cooked, thinly sliced, and assembled on a large tortilla with fresh vegetables and sauces, then cut in half to show the interior. A playful, high-energy cooking demo set to electronic music.

reels.title: Chronic Pain Relief — Dr. Sood
reels.summary: Dr. Kunal Sood, MD, stands in scrubs in a living room under the caption 'They did their research': on-screen text explains that tylenol is for generalized pain, ibuprofen decreases inflammation, gabapentin calms nerve pain, and flexeril is a muscle relaxant. The audio — a calm voice saying 'Someone cooked here' — is unrelated, giving the educational meme a surreal, humorous edge.

reels.title: Crystal Lake Cafe — San Gabriel Mountains Escape
reels.summary: A showcase of the Crystal Lake Cafe and Trading Post in the San Gabriel Mountains, Angeles National Forest — about 6,000 feet elevation and roughly an hour from Los Angeles — with foggy shots of the rustic red-doored cafe, carved wooden bear statues, pine forests, and nearby Crystal Lake. The caption recommends comfort food like Adam's signature Trading Post chili, burgers, homemade brownies and banana-nut bread, plus hiking and camping at Crystal Lake Campground, with possible bear sightings and snowy winters.

reels.title: HomePlace Furniture & Design — Store Showcase
reels.summary: A woman tests a brown leather recliner and matching sofa at HomePlace Furniture & Design's Portland showroom, demonstrating the recliner's full reclining function. A calm product showcase of the store's furniture collections set to low-frequency electronic music.

reels.title: Jalandhari Raan — Tandoori Leg of Mutton
reels.summary: @foodelhi savors the 'Jalandhari raan' by @angad693 — an extra-tender tandoori leg of mutton served in an envelope of masala — tearing naan into the curry sauce with enthusiastic two-thumbs-up approval. Tasted at one of Angad's Delhi pop-ups, it's also available at his restaurant @paratofficial.

reels.title: Going-to-the-Sun Road — Glacier National Park
reels.summary: A POV drive along the Going-to-the-Sun Road in Glacier National Park, framed as 'the most scenic road in the USA': sunset mountain views, a long tunnel, and an expansive valley panorama, set to 'The Final Countdown.' Per the caption (accurate as of Sept 2023), driving it requires a reservation at recreation.gov or arriving before 6am / after 3pm.
reels.creator_name: George & Crissa Prieto | Adventure Travel Couple

reels.title: Protein Food Hacks: Rice, Eggs & Chicken
reels.summary: Cory shares four cooking hacks to boost protein: cook rice in bone broth instead of water (+~19g protein, plus glutamine and glycine), add cottage cheese to scrambled eggs for creaminess (+~15g), marinate chicken in yogurt to keep it tender (+~15g), and add a scoop of unflavored collagen powder to coffee (no taste/texture change, +~10g). Each hack is demonstrated with clear text overlays.

reels.title: Coingrams — Trading Alerts (Crypto, Stocks, Options)
reels.summary: A reel from @coingrams promoting trading alerts covering crypto, stocks, and options; no further detail is available from the caption or visuals.

reels.title: National Parks Bucket List — Adventure Travel
reels.summary: After visiting 30 national parks, @travelwithdalt shares his awestruck reactions in a rapid-fire montage: Devils Tower, Sequoia's giant sequoias, the Badlands, North Cascades' mountain lake, Olympic's mossy forest, Glacier's cliffside lake, and Channel Islands' ocean cliffs. Captions like 'Is this real...' and 'So this is the edge of it all' pair with epic orchestral music in a save-worthy bucket-list post.

reels.title: Highway 395: Bishop to Lake Tahoe — Favorite CA Drive
reels.summary: Asya calls Highway 395 — particularly the Bishop-to-Lake Tahoe stretch — her favorite drive in California, playfully denying the alpine-looking footage is Switzerland, Italy, or Canada before revealing it's California, all under a long unsettling electronic tone for absurdist effect. The caption lists stops along 395: Mono Lake, Crowley Lake, Hot Creek Geologic Site, and Bodie.

reels.title: 5 Nonfiction Books Recommended by Nat Eliason
reels.summary: NOTE: this record's title/creator (books video by @booksforthewise) appear swapped with the reel below — the actual video and caption here are the acoustic-panel tutorial. A step-by-step tutorial installing a large decorative sound-absorbing wall panel: two men lift the heavy wavy slatted panel — dark and light brown vertical slats forming an abstract pattern, sold as 'artwork to make your room sound cozy' — position it against a white wall and adjust it from a stepladder. Set to the Rolling Stones' 'The Last Time' for the classic mismatched-audio effect.

reels.title: Fix a Hollow-Sounding Room With Acoustic Treatment
reels.summary: NOTE: this record's title/creator (acoustic treatment by @maxakustik) appear swapped with the reel above — the actual video and caption here are the books list. A man lists five nonfiction books he wishes he could read for the first time again, holding each up with a personal take: 'Gödel, Escher, Bach' (excellent payoff), 'Antifragile' (changed his view of work and risk), 'Letters from a Stoic,' 'Four Thousand Weeks' (healthier thinking about time), and 'Finite and Infinite Games' (questioning the rules of life). The caption credits the list to @nat_eliason.

reels.title: Google's TextFX — AI Toolkit for Rappers & Songwriters
reels.summary: A creator in a black hoodie and cap explains Google's TextFX, the AI toolkit for rappers and songwriters built with Lupe Fiasco for Google Labs (2023). He stresses it's not AI writing songs for you but a suite of 10 wordplay tools, demoing 'Explode' (breaking 'marauder' into similar-sounding phrases), 'Fuse' (linking 'library' and 'graveyard' with meaning), and his favorite 'Unexpect' (wild variations on 'a glass of water,' like a magic eight ball for lyrics). Tools shown include Scene, Chain, POV, Acronym, Alliteration, Fuse, Unexpect, and Unfold — framed as AI as collaborator, not crutch.

reels.title: How to Light an Interview: Three-Point Setup
reels.summary: Aputure's quick demo of lighting an interview with classic three-point lighting — fewer lights, faster moves — by @madebylonevalley, using the new Light Dome III and Light Dome Mini III to soften the key light. The caption's rule for corporate/documentary interview lighting: keep it simple and move with speed.

reels.title: Oregon Coast Road Trip
reels.summary: A short road-trip post calling a drive down the Oregon coast one of the best routes in the U.S. — a reset-and-get-inspired travel moment; the caption offers no further detail.

reels.title: 10 Affordable Starter Watches
reels.summary: A structured guide to '10 of the best starter watches under $150': G-Shock (durability), Orient Bambino (classic automatic dress watch), Orient Mako and Ray (affordable, 200m water resistance), Orient Kamasu (sapphire crystal), Citizen Eco-Drive Garrison (solar-powered, super accurate), Seiko 5, and Casio digitals including the F91W, A700, and AE-1200 World Time. Presented with close-ups and a brief positive take on each.

reels.title: Ambrogio by Acquerello — La Jolla Tasting Menu
reels.summary: A promo for Ambrogio by Acquerello in La Jolla, home to Chef Silvio (Michelin-starred through his career): two 8-course tasting menus — fully vegetarian ($139) or meat/fish ($159) — fusing Italian, Korean, and Californian influences, with dishes like Italian ramen and Hokkaido scallops with gold. The creator calls it possibly the best restaurant in La Jolla, with gorgeous plating and an extensive wine vault — perfect for special occasions.

reels.title: Movie Road, Lone Pine — Famous California Drive
reels.summary: An aerial clip follows a black SUV down Movie Road in Lone Pine, CA — 'one of the most famous drives in California' — through desert rock formations toward snow-capped mountains at golden hour, set to lo-fi hip-hop. The caption notes it's a dirt road and asks visitors to Leave No Trace (and pick up trash they find).
reels.creator_name: 𝐈 & 𝐁 || 𝐇𝐢𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 | 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐯𝐞𝐥 | 𝐍𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐬

reels.title: British Library Flickr Gems for Mixed-Media Art
reels.summary: Karl Shakur shows how the British Library's Flickr page offers a huge free library of public-domain images — scientific illustrations, old comic books, and more — usable for personal and commercial mixed-media art. He notes the moon sequence in the video took him under 45 minutes to make, urging viewers to imagine what's possible with more time.

reels.title: Garage Collective — San Diego Car Club
reels.summary: A promo for Garage Collective, a San Diego/Coronado car community for enthusiasts, highlighting curated member events, track days, group drives, and cars-and-coffee meets, with a free tour bookable via the link in bio for prospective members.

reels.title: 4 LA Restaurants on the Michelin Bib Gourmand List
reels.summary: A quick food-news hit: the Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand list just came out with 4 LA restaurants on it; the reel itself names none further in the caption.

reels.title: Top 5 Scenic Drives in California (Blog)
reels.summary: A compilation of California scenic drives — Pacific Coast Highway's cliffside tunnel, a forest road (likely Avenue of the Giants), and towering redwoods — set to an AI voiceover and hip-hop. It promotes Asya's blog post compiling her top-5 scenic California drives after five years of driving the state, linked in bio.

reels.title: Tag Them If You Want That Money Back — Meme
reels.summary: A relatable meme: 'The insta stories of the friend who owes you money,' cutting between a cocktail in a garden, a lavish high-end meal, and a luxury car ride — lavish posturing set to dark hip-hop. Caption: 'Tag them if you want that money back' (inspo @thelensof_t).

reels.title: Streaming Guide: 5 Must-Watch Hindi Films
reels.summary: A streaming guide to five underrated Hindi films, counted down 5 to 1 with clips and brief analysis: 'Taxi No. 9211' (Disney+ Hotstar), 'Yuva' (Netflix), 'Shaitan' (Netflix), 'Sandeep aur Pinky Faraar' (Prime Video), and 'Black Friday' (Disney+ Hotstar). By Ahona (@buanosnoches) for Humans of Cinema.

reels.title: What Size Should Your Bedroom Rug Be?
reels.summary: A design tip answering 'What size should your bedroom rug be?' — like a tray grouping objects, a rug visually anchors furniture so the room reads as a collection.

reels.title: South Eastern Idaho Road Trip Itinerary
reels.summary: A southeastern Idaho road-trip itinerary starting in Boise and heading to Idaho Falls: Craters of the Moon and Shoshone Ice Caves en route, then the Idaho Falls Greenbelt for strolling or biking, with more stops in the full caption.
reels.creator_name: Katie • Travel & Lifestyle Creator • Based in Idaho

reels.title: 10 Stops: San Francisco to Seattle Road Trip
reels.summary: A 10-stop San Francisco-to-Seattle road-trip itinerary in a calm travel vlog: redwoods, Muir Beach Overlook, Russian Gulch State Park, Avenue of the Giants, Fern Canyon, Bandon (southern Oregon coast), Crater Lake National Park, Silver Falls State Park, Columbia River Gorge, Gifford Pinchot National Forest, and Mount Rainier National Park, set to mellow lo-fi hip-hop.
reels.creator_name: DANNY & DANIE | travel | hiking | road trips

reels.title: 6 Favorite Tools for Building a Bag Brand
reels.summary: Zack Kravits shares six tools he uses to build his bag brand: 'Logo Modernism' (logo inspiration), 'Dictionary of Color Combinations' (color theory), the Milanote app (organizing visual ideas), the Superfuture website (interior/showroom inspiration), Pinterest (general inspiration), and DeathToStock (high-quality stock photos) — physical resources linked in the caption.

reels.title: Oregon's Highway of Waterfalls — Highway 138
reels.summary: A serene vlog along Oregon's Highway 138 through Umpqua National Forest — 'the most underrated Oregon road trip' — featuring over 15 waterfalls including Toketee, Watson, Whitehorse, and Lemolo Falls, plus hot springs and the Mount Bailey trail, set to slow ambient music.
reels.creator_name: Gwyn and Ami Manser | PNW + USA adventure travel

reels.title: Oregon Coast Road Trip Itinerary
reels.summary: A labeled Oregon Coast itinerary — Cannon Beach, Oswald West State Park (Indian Sands Beach, Cape Falcon), Thor's Well, Yaquina Head and Heceta Head Lighthouses (the latter bookable overnight in the caretaker's house), the Oregon Dunes, and the Samuel H. Boardman Scenic Corridor — oddly scored with a deep, suspenseful voiceover and dark ambient music that gives the peaceful footage an ominous, meme-like twist.

reels.title: 9-Day Oregon & Washington Road Trip
reels.summary: Kat Bennett's 1,200-mile, 9-day Oregon & Washington itinerary: arrive in Portland and rent a car; Silver Falls State Park, then the Oregon coast; drive the coast to Coos Bay (Oregon Dunes, Cape Perpetua); Bend for hiking — with scenic shots of coastal cliffs, waterfalls, snow-capped peaks, and a turquoise glacial lake, all under a low synthesized drone for a cinematic feel.
reels.creator_name: KAT BENNETT | Adventure Travel & Group Trips

reels.title: Brookings & Samuel H. Boardman — Oregon Coast
reels.summary: A meditative Oregon coast clip — likely Cape Perpetua's mossy rock arch over churning blue-green water — paired with the quote 'Better to have a short life that is full of what you like doing than a long life spent in a miserable way' and mellow lo-fi. Kev and the creator had dreamed of visiting for four years, urging viewers to add Brookings and the Samuel H. Boardman corridor to their Oregon list.

reels.title: Sawtooth Scenic Byway, Idaho
reels.summary: @visitidaho's serene tour of the Sawtooth Scenic Byway: aerial mountain roads, a river valley, a deep-blue lake among evergreens, autumn foliage, and two elk behind a wooden fence — 'rugged mountain peaks and starry starry nights,' set to slow ambient music.

reels.title: Famous Paintings Depicting Death
reels.summary: A 'Death by Different Painters' meme: Dali's photo opens a sequence of paintings on the theme of death — Albert Edelfelt's 'A Child's Convoy,' Zdzislaw Beksinski's 'Death Valley,' Gustav Klimt's 'Death and Life,' Jacques-Louis David's work, and more — set to a somber sustained tone for a humorous-satirical take on the motif.

reels.title: Tesla: Be Alone — That's When Ideas Are Born
reels.summary: An inspirational edit on Nikola Tesla's ode to solitude — 'The mind is sharper and keener in seclusion and uninterrupted solitude' — illustrated with Tesla in his lab, a student studying alone, a lone cliffside walker, and a floating cityscape, closing on 'Be alone, that is when ideas are born.'

reels.title: Bang Bang Chicken Skewers
reels.summary: Day 17 of her 30-day air fryer series: bang bang chicken skewers combining two of her popular recipes. Boneless skinless chicken thighs are cubed and marinated in mayo, sweet chili sauce, sriracha, paprika, garlic and onion powder, salt, and lime juice; threaded onto wooden skewers; air-fried until golden and crispy; then brushed with bang bang sauce. She suggests serving with coconut rice.

reels.title: Learning Dramatic Portraits From Chris Knight
reels.summary: Day 20 of Nishkam's 30-day challenge: his experience learning dramatic portraits from Chris Knight's class — full insights on lighting, how to use and control it — which he says was worth every second and is a must for aspiring magazine or advertising photographers, with even pros attending. Link in bio to his @photobasics profile.

reels.title: Chef Coskun Abik — SF Restaurateur Honored by Mayor
reels.summary: A vlog by Josh Kun — introduced as owner of San Francisco's Blind Butcher — announcing he's being recognized by the mayor. He runs four small businesses: Blind Butcher (modern American, Castro), Lark (Greek, next door), Dunya (Mediterranean, Polk Street), and Moka Coffee (coffee shop next to Dunya). He tours Blind Butcher's dishes — octapodaki, Brussels sprouts, lamb lollipops, Wagyu burger, branzino — and declares the rosemary-oregano marinated prime ribeye with chimichurri his final-meal choice.

reels.title: Kodi Bengare, Udupi — A Quieter Alternative to Parra Road
reels.summary: XPLORE The Earth spotlights Kodi Bengare (Kodi Bengre) in Udupi, Karnataka — a scenic coastal road to the Delta Point lined with coconut trees, beaches, and river views — as a quieter alternative to Goa's over-touristed Parra Road. With maps and photos, the creator urges: travel responsibly, don't pose for pictures on the road, just explore and be in the moment (visuals shot from a safe spot after parking the scooter).

reels.title: Cheap Watches That Actually Look Good
reels.summary: A host calling himself 'The Man' reviews affordable watches that look good: the Casio G-Shock (rugged, colorful, customizable straps/bezels, under $200), the Orient Bambino (classic open-heart dress watch with mechanical movement), and the Tissot PRX Quartz (Royal Oak/Nautilus-adjacent design, pre-owned under $250, many dial colors).

reels.title: The Best Socks Money Can Buy
reels.summary: Nolan Daniel White counts down the 'five best socks money can buy,' spotlighting four on screen: William Ellery (hiking socks), American Trench (classic casual), Organic Threads (value pick), and Anonymouism (Japanese-made socks with unique yarns) — with notes on each brand's quality, style, and origin.

reels.title: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway — SoCal Bucket List
reels.summary: A ride up the Palm Springs Aerial Tramway — from the base station past towering mountains to the summit — with panoramic views of valleys and peaks from the tram's big windows. @socalnation calls it a must-add to the SoCal bucket list.

reels.title: Humanize ChatGPT's Writing With One Line
reels.summary: Uncover AI's tutorial for making ChatGPT emails sound human: many find ChatGPT rewrites too formal or too casual, so the fix is the prompt line 'TONE: CONVERSATIONAL, SPARTAN, USE LESS CORPORATE JARGON.' He demonstrates it on an overly formal email after showing a Reddit post of someone struggling with the same issue — a practical tip for professionals using AI for communication.
reels.creator_name: AI Tools & News | Technology | Artificial Intelligence

reels.title: Flynn the Goat — Breaking Bad Funny Tee
reels.summary: A woman in a kitchen shows off a black tee with a 'Walt Jr.' graphic — a 'Flynn the goat' nod to Breaking Bad's Walter White Jr. — set to a confident hip-hop track for the classic ironic merch-showcase effect. #notsafeforwear #funnytshirts.

reels.title: Fable AI Generated a South Park Episode With AI
reels.summary: A high-energy explainer on Fable's 'The Simulation' — an AI platform that generates entire animated shows: trained on thousands of character/background images, it builds a virtual world of AI 'bots' that roam and interact, so one prompt produces characters, dialogue, voices, and editing for a full episode. The South Park demo was research-only; Fable plans original shows later in the year. Caption: 'Animated content just changed forever.'

reels.title: Midcentury Modern Loft Interior
reels.summary: A showcase of a midcentury modern loft interior — Eames, USM, Saarinen, Noguchi, Neutra, and Frank Lloyd Wright pieces among the hashtags — captioned 'If barbie loves it I love it too.'

reels.title: The 'Pablo Picasso Strategy' for Reverse-Engineering Brands
reels.summary: A business-strategy reel explaining how to use the 'Pablo Picasso Strategy' to reverse-engineer successful brands; the caption gives no further detail.

reels.title: French Pav — French Toast With Pav & Old Monk Butter
reels.summary: Saransh Goila's 'French Pav' — a French-toast-meets-pav fusion celebrating France's UPI integration as sweet Indo-French 'dosti.' He makes 'Old Monk butter' by browning and whipping butter with melted chocolate, soaks pav in a spiced eggy mixture, toasts it, and assembles the decadent sandwich, noting you can 'add or subtract butter depending on how French you are.'

reels.title: Chicken in Dahi (Yogurt) Curry
reels.summary: Chicken in Dahi curry — 'a completely made up name' — with ginger-garlic paste as the constant base. A homemade, protein-forward chicken curry recipe reel; the caption is mostly hashtags.

reels.title: Mike Tyson x Muhammad Ali Boxing Meme
reels.summary: 'Hit 💀' — a Mike Tyson × Muhammad Ali boxing meme set to Punjabi music, a quick follow-for-more comedy clip.

reels.title: Tomato-Garlic Chutney With Methi Parantha
reels.summary: Rachna's viral tamatar-lehsun ki chutney with khasta masoori methi parantha, pitched as a weight-loss-friendly, easy, quick recipe. First-person tutorial: halve tomatoes, roast them in a grill pan with 1 tbsp butter, roast 2–3 garlic cloves in 1 tbsp oil, combine with onions and spices for the chutney; then knead, roll, and griddle the paratha until golden and crispy.

reels.title: Data Scientist vs Data Analyst vs ML Engineer — Roles Explained
reels.summary: Srikanth Varma (co-founder, Applied Roots) breaks down five data/AI roles in a studio interview: data analyst (cleans raw data, makes sense of it with basic stats and plotting); data scientist (an analyst plus the wider spectrum — ML and deep learning); ML engineer (50% data scientist, 50% software engineer); applied scientist (bleeding-edge depth applied to hard problems); research scientist (pushes research boundaries, e.g. Facebook AI Research, Google DeepMind).

reels.title: How to Season a Wok — 7 Steps
reels.summary: A concise wok-seasoning tutorial: 1) wash the wok with soap and water; 2) heat on a gas stove from all sides until bluish; 3) coat with oil; 4) add water to lift excess oil and impurities, then wipe clean; 5) heat again, oil again, wipe excess; 6) add sliced onions to burn and finish seasoning. Clear on-screen text for each step.

reels.title: King of Drummers — AI Surrealist Art
reels.summary: An AI-generated dark-surrealist music video 'King of Drummers' (editor cut): a hyper-muscular, pale crowned figure in red cloth plays an ornate golden drum kit in a gothic cathedral hall, drenched in blood-like red liquid pooling on the marble floor — painterly Midjourney/Disco Diffusion style — set to an upbeat classic-rock track about riding high. No dialogue; caption credits @emilvergo.

reels.title: Top 20 Most Disturbing Movies — Part 4
reels.summary: The finale (part 4 of 4) of Bryce Vaughn's 'Top 20 Most Disturbing Films I've Ever Seen,' counting down 5→1 from a comment reply: 'Antichrist,' 'Pink Flamingos,' 'The Human Centipede 2,' 'Martyrs,' and 'A Serbian Film' — with clips on his laptop and an explicit warning about the films' extremity, especially A Serbian Film.

reels.title: Top 20 Most Disturbing Movies — Part 3
reels.summary: Part 3 of Bryce Vaughn's 'Top 20 Most Disturbing Films I've Ever Seen': 'Soft & Quiet,' 'Cannibal Holocaust,' 'Jacob's Ladder,' 'Eraserhead,' and 'I Spit on Your Grave' — each with a brief description of what makes it disturbing, shown via clips on his laptop in a serious, suspenseful tone.

reels.title: How I Became a Race Car Driver in Japan — Part 3
reels.summary: Part three of how @hanubuu_ became a race car driver in Japan, with thanks to @arisa_mizuhara and @ishiihiro1988 and an invite for questions.

reels.title: 4 Exercises for Better Posture & Less Back Pain
reels.summary: POV-style fitness reel: 'you started doing these 4 exercises on a regular basis and now your posture is better & upper back pain is gone' — 4 posture/back-pain exercises (not named in caption) with #posturecorrection #spinemobility.

reels.title: Why Stable Diffusion Beats Midjourney (ControlNet)
reels.summary: A reel arguing why Stable Diffusion beats Midjourney — ControlNet is free to try. No further detail in the caption.

reels.title: The Only 10 Exercises Men Need to Build Muscle
reels.summary: 'ONLY 10 EXERCISES MEN NEED TO BUILD A MUSCLE' — a bodybuilding reel featuring @cbum and @chriswillx (Modern Wisdom podcast, Gold's Gym Venice); the exercises aren't listed in the caption.

reels.title: Restock Alert: 8' Faux Fiddle Leaf Tree
reels.summary: Restock alert for the 8' faux fiddle leaf fig from Amazon: it ships in two pieces that need fluffing, and she styles it with green artificial moss and a small white round LED light at the base for a cozy glow. Always green, sells out fast — shoppable on her storefront under 'plants.'

reels.title: Laila Majnu Quote — Bollywood Cinema Edit
reels.summary: A Bollywood cinema edit built around Qais's Laila Majnu dialogue — 'Tujhe kya lagta hai yeh hum kar rahe hain. Humari kahani likhi hui hai, aur yeh duniya kya, duniya ke log kya, hum khud bhi use nahi badal sakte' (audio by @shubhamdead, inspired by @amusingbeing), with Imtiaz Ali film hashtags.

reels.title: Art History Hot Take
reels.summary: Dan Rosen's satirical hot take naming the 'three most overrated artists of the 20th century': Salvador Dalí, Francis Bacon, and Mark Rothko — paintings overlaid on screen, delivered as a provocative 'this is just like, my opinion man' listicle.

reels.title: Cristiano Ronaldo-Inspired Abs Workout
reels.summary: Bernardo Rebeil's Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired abs workout: a shirtless circuit demo of leg lifts, heel touches, suitcase crunches, elbow-to-knee crunches, and toe touches, with reps on screen and instructions matching the moves — repeat the circuit four times.

reels.title: Exquisite Desk Setup Tour
reels.summary: An exquisite desk setup tour — 'every item on the desktop should be exquisite and designed' (an ashtray is tagged); a short design eye-candy clip.

reels.title: The Life Resume Formula: Misogi + 6 Trips + Quarterly Habits
reels.summary: Jesse Itzler's 'life resume' formula, mid-2023: #1 Misogi — one year-defining annual challenge (he launched a podcast in 2022 after quitting smoking); #2 'Kevin's Rule' — six mini-adventures a year, after a happy friend who takes his 8-year-old kids to climb Mount Washington in winter every other month (240 experiences by 80); #3 one winning habit per quarter, like 10 minutes of daily meditation. Six adventures + one killer experience + four habits a year means you 'win life.'

reels.title: 100M Views Thank-You — SRK Fan Video
reels.summary: Ibrahim Qadri's 100M-views thank-you: the Shah Rukh Khan impersonator, in black shirt, cargo pants, white shoes, sunglasses, and SRK-style curls, holds the iconic arms-outstretched pose while a smiling Delhi Airport security officer does a routine pat-down with a metal detector — then shakes hands, smiles, and blows a kiss to the camera, set to an upbeat Hindi film song.

reels.title: Biggest Lesson Training With the NFL's Fittest
reels.summary: Pierce Showe on the biggest thing he's learned working out with 2x 'Fittest Man in NFL' @weatherford5 — a running/fitness motivation reel; the lesson itself isn't spelled out in the caption.

reels.title: From the Archives: The Great Indian LSD Trip (Om-Dar-B-Dar)
reels.summary: IFP × Aarsh Limbadia (@cinecuration) 'From the Archives' review of Kamal Swaroop's 1982 psychedelic film 'Om-Dar-B-Dar' — 'The Great Indian LSD Trip': a convention-shattering, avant-garde work ahead of its time, with the note that Swaroop assisted Richard Attenborough on Gandhi.

reels.title: Meta's MusicGen — AI Music Generation (Free on Hugging Face)
reels.summary: Overpowered demos Meta's MusicGen — 'Midjourney for music,' free on Hugging Face. In split screen, a presenter shows text-to-music generation ('an Indian hip hop beat, using guitar riffs') and style transfer, turning the Harry Potter theme into an Indian fusion with sitar, tabla, and flute.

reels.title: Maal pienge — Bollywood Meme
reels.summary: A Bollywood meme compilation: candid clips of celebrities set to a deep-voiced 'The secret of there energy' audio over a pulsing electronic beat — a bait-and-switch where the mysterious setup dissolves into mundane visuals. Captioned 'Maal pienge — just for fun, don't take it seriously.'

reels.title: Howie Day — Poetry Post
reels.summary: A Howie Day poetry post — a short music/poetry clip with a hit-like-and-comment CTA and explore-page hashtags; no further detail.

reels.title: Premier Tourist Hotspots in India — Andaman
reels.summary: An interview clip where Raj Shamani names Havelock Island in the Andamans as his favorite Indian destination: Radhanagar Beach lets you walk half a kilometer into turquoise water (waist-to-chest deep, famously soft sand), ranked among the world's top 10 beaches, plus nearby Neil Island — 'beautiful and still largely untouched.' Posted by @thrivewith_bhaskar (Makemytrip/Deep Kalra reference).

reels.title: Travel movie recs to watch before your next trip
reels.summary: Dill, a solo traveler, is finally watching "the backpacker bible" before her upcoming backpacking trip — The Secret Life of Walter Mitty — and wants to see what the hype is about. She presents it as a must-watch for anyone traveling soon, framing it as essential pre-trip viewing.

reels.title: Virtual Ladakh road trip in an off-road mobile game
reels.summary: Presenter Karan Singh promotes the mobile game Offroad League Online as "a Ladakh trip inside a game," using a split-screen of his studio pitch and in-game footage. He highlights the open-world environment, multiplayer rescue mechanics (pulling stuck friends out), vehicle customization, and custom maps, with footage of a Tesla Cybertruck conquering muddy trails. The pitch: go on a virtual Ladakh trip with friends and create moments that feel real.

reels.title: 13 must-see stops on Canada's Icefields Parkway
reels.summary: Shahbaz showcases Canada's Icefields Parkway, "the most scenic drive in the world" — 230 km (140 miles) between Lake Louise and Jasper through towering peaks, turquoise lakes, ancient glaciers, and wildlife. His list of 13 must-see stops starts with Lake Louise, Herbert Lake for mirror-like reflections, and Bow Lake, paired with the text overlay: "a road everyone should take once in their lifetime."

reels.title: Best Indian restaurant in NYC? (Beli rec)
reels.summary: Dev Sahuja plays a this-or-that game of NYC Indian restaurants on Beli: Bungalow over Junoon (citing chef Vikas Khanna), Dhamaka over Adda (for the fresh paneer), and Semma over Adda (for the gunpowder dosa). His co-host also picks Dhamaka, landing on Bungalow, Dhamaka, and Semma as the top recommendations for the best Indian food in NYC.

reels.title: Best mystery crime thrillers — watchlist
reels.summary: Liam Saul counts down his favorite mystery crime thrillers, calling The Clovehitch Killer "dark and twisted" and The Order "one of my favorite films from last year," before revealing Super Dark Times as his number-one pick. He asks viewers to share their own favorite crime dramas in the comments.

reels.title: Abhishek Banerjee: 'The biggest fear of an artist are limits'
reels.summary: In this Bombay Journey clip from Mashable India, Abhishek Banerjee says an artist's biggest fear is limits — being typecast. He describes being offered dark roles like Paatal Lok and Apurva, then being taken aback by the sheer number of quirky characters coming his way, and reflects on navigating the industry's expectations around his casting.
reels.creator_name: Mashable India | A Fork Media Group Co.

reels.title: My design stack — what's yours?
reels.summary: A non-technical founder films himself in a park sharing his five-tool "design stack" for building a tech product without a designer: Mobbin for user flows, Figma for UI design, Lucide for icons, WhatFont for typography, and Khroma for color palettes. He closes by promoting his own smart renting app and asking viewers to follow for daily content — noting he wouldn't recommend filming on the floor under a tree as it got dark.

reels.title: 3-day NorCal road trip: Shasta, Burney Falls, Lassen
reels.summary: Tannya Cai lays out her favorite whirlwind 3-day NorCal road trip covering Shasta, Burney Falls, and Lassen, with stops including Lake Shasta Caverns, Castle Crags, McCloud Falls, Burney Falls, Cinder Cone, Lake Helen, Bumpass Hell, and Sulfur Works. The star is the 1.5-mile hike to Heart Lake (Castle Lake) — her "best ROI hike in California" for its free parking and panoramic Mount Shasta view. She stresses Leave No Trace and offers a free California mini-guide to anyone who comments WANDER.
reels.creator_name: Tannya Cai | adventure • travel • photography • drone

reels.title: Mind-disturbing Bollywood thriller pick
reels.summary: Jay Raval posts a clip he calls a "mind disturbing" Bollywood thriller, and the comments collectively identify it as 12 o'clock — a low-budget horror featuring a possessed girl who speaks in a male voice. Commenters roast it as unscary and poorly executed (noting an IMDb rating of 3.2 and an RGV connection), with some joking the possession scene made them laugh, turning the recommendation into a shared joke about bad cinema.

reels.title: 72 hours in Ojai & Santa Barbara
reels.summary: Codi Musler recaps a 72-hour Ojai and Santa Barbara weekend: Ojai Olive Oil Company (19 olive oils and vinegars tasted), Heavenly Honey (10+ varieties, buying lavender and clove), the world's largest outdoor bookshop Bart's Books, and Ojai Ice Cream — followed by a chaotic hotel check-in. In Santa Barbara: dinner at The Lark, Mother Dough bagels, a tri-tip sandwich with live music at Cold Spring Tavern, Happy Canyon wine tasting in Los Olivos, steak and tableside tiramisu at Marisella in the Ritz-Carlton, dolphins spotted from Miramar Beach, and shakshuka at Field & Fort in Summerland.

reels.title: Wah Jee Wah: Indian barbecue on a charcoal grill in Hayward
reels.summary: Revi raves about Wah Jee Wah in Hayward (32681 Mission Blvd), an Indian barbecue spot cooking over a real open-flame charcoal grill. Standouts: the lamb dipped in tikka masala sauce ("a problem"), the masala mac and cheese with a long cheese pull ("good enough to make you cry"), plus grilled shrimp, tofu, and chicken tikka. Chef Ron shares his personal cooking history and his father's restaurant, saying the joy of watching customers enjoy the food is "something money can't buy."

reels.title: Smash burger in a paratha bun at Klay by Karak House
reels.summary: foodfindsuae spotlights Klay by Karak House in The Dubai Mall and its paratha smash burger: a freshly prepared, fluffed paratha bun stacked with double smashed beef patties, caramelized onion, and cheese for AED 39 — "the combination goes hard." The butter chicken paratha bun is equally recommended, and the verdict is to wash it all down with karak.

reels.title: 6 San Diego hidden gem food spots
reels.summary: Laura shares her go-to San Diego hidden gems for brunch, date night, and casual eats: Konito's Cafe for French toast, breakfast burritos, and "unreal" cheesy potatoes; Juan Jasper for date night (a tiny no-reservations spot worth the wait); Michi Michi for rotating pastries like the huevos rancheros danish; Ujin for truffle-infused ramen; Leilani's Cafe for loco moco; and Good Measure, a new brunch spot with standout sandwiches and waffles — spanning North Park, UTC, Golden Hill, and Bankers Hill.

reels.title: Unico Coffee: hip-hop coffee shop hidden in North Park
reels.summary: Marissa walks through a graffiti-covered alley in North Park to Unico Coffee (@unicocoffeeco), a hip-hop themed coffee shop that's "not your typical coffee shop": graffiti-covered walls, an open-air bar, a corrugated metal ceiling strung with lights, specialty espresso, and DJ sets. It's the brick-and-mortar follow-up from the friend behind her earlier viral vintage-car-with-a-coffee-machine-in-the-trunk video.

reels.title: AI tool drop — comment 'Dev' for the link
reels.summary: Vishnu Vijayan demos Orchid, a YC-backed no-code tool he says is "changing the no-code game" with "premium, human and futuristic" design output versus "vibeless, copy-paste looking" competitors. He builds a website by describing it and clicking "Clone," then customizes backgrounds (a rocket taking off) and spins up a flying-car-service landing page and an urban-transport booking app — touting clean UI components, no outdated templates, a visual editor, fast deployment, and responsive-by-default design. Viewers comment "Dev" to get the link.

reels.title: Dreamy reel from San Diego's best Italian restaurant
reels.summary: Marisi gives a POV tour of a dreamy open-air San Diego Italian restaurant patio — past a decorative metal gate into a sun-dappled space with a latticed ceiling, a big leafy tree, round light-wood tables, and patterned terracotta-and-cream tile strung with globe lights. The joke is the jarring audio: a somber classical piece laid over the serene visuals, an ironic contrast that turns the pretty tour into absurdist comedy. Caption: "feels like you're in a dream ✨."

reels.title: Disturbing found-footage horror picks
reels.summary: Chuck Shaughnessy lists 10 "fucked up" found footage horror films, introducing each with its poster and a brief, hyperbolic description of its disturbing content. The split-screen format keeps him on one side and the posters on the other in a high-energy horror recommendation rundown — each pick "messed up in its own kind of way."

reels.title: The art of composition in cinematography
reels.summary: A short visual piece from Sirence Studios on the art of composition in cinematography, tagged as filmed in the Azores on Sony gear — the caption is the entire message, with no spoken narration or additional detail.

reels.title: Black Narcissus (1947): Powell & Pressburger's Technicolor masterpiece
reels.summary: Cinema Of The World presents Black Narcissus (1947), Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger's psychological drama about Anglican nuns whose mission to establish a school and hospital unravels as isolation and buried desires take their toll. The cinematic clip — a robed figure ringing a great bell on a cliff edge under dramatic orchestral music — carries the overlay "This is the most beautiful film you will ever watch," a tribute to the film's Technicolor visual mastery.

reels.title: Relatable parenting humor: 'I wish I was kidding'
reels.summary: Kelly Totoraitis does a short, self-deprecating skit on social anxiety: the idealized, confident self ("How I think I look when I socialize") versus the relaxed, joyful reality. The ironic use of slow, melancholic background music amplifies the joke — everyone has a social-anxiety side they pretend doesn't exist. Caption: "I wish I was kidding."

reels.title: Why Willem Dafoe walked away from remaking Onibaba
reels.summary: akashmall recounts how Willem Dafoe acquired the remake rights to the Japanese horror classic Onibaba out of deep reverence — then walked away, realizing "it's so specific to its time" and that "any time I tried to put a spin on it, I ruined the source material." The anecdote is set against eerie, high-contrast visuals of a Hannya-masked figure and a terrified woman fleeing through a dark forest.

reels.title: Khadpanch web series review: the darkest truth of Punjab
reels.summary: Movies Radio (Troll Punjabi) reviews the Punjabi web series Khadpanch, a dark murder mystery about the "darkest truth of Punjab": drug addiction, extramarital affairs, fake milk and alcohol businesses, and village-level corruption. He highlights its cinematic depiction of Punjab's underbelly, flashes an 8.7 IMDb rating on screen, and notes the series is free on YouTube in both Punjabi and a Hindi dub.

reels.title: Untitled reel from a documentary creator
reels.summary: Christie Boschman shares the documentary A Cursed Man, which follows a man who believes he's afflicted by a series of curses as he travels to an Indian jungle, a Mexican cave, and various urban settings seeking help from witches and spiritual practitioners. The film intersperses the blonde narrator's on-camera hosting with interviews about black magic and ritual practices, and carries a disclaimer warning viewers the creators aren't responsible for any negative effects. Per community comments, it's available on Amazon Prime in the US for a fee.

reels.title: Know your rights + ICE rapid response hotlines
reels.summary: Tommy Marcus posts a CBS News clip from an immigration-raids protest in Downtown LA where, asked about tear gas, he quips "It tasted like fascism." His caption is a practical resource: rapid-response hotlines for LA (888-624-4752), Long Beach Órale (562-276-0267), Riverside & San Bernardino (909-361-4588), and Orange County (714-881-1558), plus Know Your Rights basics — don't open the door without a signed federal warrant, you can stay silent, don't sign anything you don't understand, and you can ask for a lawyer.

reels.title: King of Mughlai & Awadhi food in Delhi
reels.summary: Shoaib Arora visits Al Rasheed Bar-Be-Que in Mount Kailash, New Delhi (CSC Complex, DDA Market), calling it the "King of Mughlai and Awadhi Food in Delhi." Proprietor Al Rasheed, in a black apron reading "THE KING OF KAKORI KABAB," mixes minced meat with cashew nuts and ladles thick red sauce while skewers grill behind him. The menu spans Kakori kabab, chicken karahi, tikka, seekh kabab, korma, reshmi kabab, galouti kabab, chicken paratha, naan, and tikka masala.

reels.title: Reagan Presidential Library in Simi Valley is worth the drive
reels.summary: Courtney Adelman tours the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library in Simi Valley, calling it "actually really interesting and cool." Highlights: the massive Boeing VC-25A Air Force One (in service 1973–2001 for seven presidents from Nixon to George W. Bush), a replica Oval Office, the Marine One helicopter, a fragment of the Berlin Wall, Lincoln Continental presidential limousines, and fighter jets — with a memorial to Ronald and Nancy Reagan noted by commenters.

reels.title: Las Ketchup — The Ketchup Song (Aserejé), Spanish version
reels.summary: Find Good Songs reposts Las Ketchup's 2002 global hit "The Ketchup Song (Aserejé)" in its Spanish version. The iconic "Aserejé" chorus is a phonetic Spanish reinterpretation of the Sugarhill Gang's "Rapper's Delight," name-dropping a character called Diego. Comments ride the nostalgia wave — the 2002 dance craze, the low-rise flared-jeans fashion of the era, and the long-running urban legend that the gibberish lyrics are satanic or a witchcraft spell.

reels.title: José Andrés' microwave omelette hack (JRE clip)
reels.summary: The meme pairs a Joe Rogan Experience clip — Rogan, in a deep gravelly voice, raving about a "microwave omelette" as the "best omelette in the history of mankind" — with completely unrelated footage of a step-by-step sandwich-making tutorial. The bait-and-switch is the joke: the earnest, hyped-up podcast audio clashes with the mundane cooking visuals. The caption frames it as Michelin-starred chef José Andrés stunning Rogan with the microwave claim.

reels.title: Don't rely on AllTrails for backcountry navigation
reels.summary: Colorado hiking guide Shelby Mann warns that AllTrails is a crowd-sourced trail directory — not a reliable backcountry navigation tool — saying it's burned her before. For off-grid trips she recommends apps built for it: @caltopo for pro-level planning and layers, @avenzamaps for PDF topo maps and printed backups, and @onxbac… The message lands with humor: serene tent footage and a slow, melancholic folk song under the text "This is going to ruffle some feathers… Remember, AllTrails is NOT a navigation app."

reels.title: 2-day Yosemite itinerary: hidden waterfalls & secret views
reels.summary: Dan Bernstein shares a free 2-day Yosemite itinerary built around the premise "Yosemite is all crowds? Think again." First the logistics: Yosemite requires entry reservations from 6am–2pm on select dates May 24–Sept 1 (Memorial Day, June 15–Aug 15, Labor Day) via Recreation.gov. The itinerary covers ten curated stops — hidden waterfalls, secret tunnel viewpoints, swim spots, wildflowers, and a family- and dog-friendly trail — with AllTrails links, preloaded Google Maps for both driving days, food recommendations, and lodging tips. Comments add: dogs are allowed on several trails, Autocamp Yosemite sits outside the park at roughly $400–$600/night, and specific spots like Foresta Falls, Diana Falls, and the Wawona water spot.
reels.creator_name: Dan Bernstein: Travel Guides | Hiking | California

reels.title: The unplanned Gladiator wheat-field shot, 25 years on
reels.summary: Filmthusiast celebrates Gladiator's 25th anniversary with Ridley Scott's anecdote about the legendary opening shot: the hand through the wheat wasn't planned — it was the last shot of principal photography in Italy, and the hand wasn't Russell Crowe's. Crowe never came to Italy; Scott spotted his double smoking in the dry mid-summer field, told him to get out of it, and filmed the hand instead.

reels.title: Most unique tattoos: 12 artists to follow
reels.summary: Tattoo ethnographer Dakota Weik rapid-fire showcases twelve artists with "most unique" work: @pashainktattoo, @nicotattoo.nyc, @hurjaesae, @maradentattoo, @dudalozanotattoo, @anshin_anshin_tattoo, @koblindeadman, @artisteph, @lilianraya, @matteonangeroni, @tattooist_fluffy, and @danmcwilliamsart — spanning glitch-realism, chrome-style designs, saturated florals, gnome motifs, and Pokémon in a Game Boy Color aesthetic. Comments pile on more names from Asia, India, Romania, and South Africa, and the post sparks conversation about racial inclusivity in tattoo culture.

reels.title: Tesla HDMI interface module install (Model 3/Y)
reels.summary: GIO demos an HDMI interface module from @evoffer.official that lets a Tesla's infotainment system play video while the car is in motion — distinct from the browser method. The night-time POV shows the central screen switching from navigation to a video player running a sports broadcast, news, and a baseball game in full- or partial-screen. It works with all Model 3 and Y; the product link is in his bio with code M3PGIO15 for a discount, and the install video is in his previous reel.

reels.title: Chins Point Loma: family-style Chinese spot
reels.summary: Helen Nguyen raves about the newly opened Point Loma location of Chin's Fine Chinese Cuisine (3373 Rosecrans) — "Can't get enough of Chins!!!" Everything is served family style, which she says she'll "never get tired of coming back" for, praising the huge selection of flavorful, affordable dishes and the friendly staff.

reels.title: Joshua Tree couples getaway tiny house
reels.summary: Desert Home Retreats showcases the "Couples Resort" in Joshua Tree — a modern black-exterior cabin with a rectangular pool, orange curved sofa, galaxy-themed mural, retro light-blue bicycles, hanging swing chairs, a pergola, and a tall wooden fence. The pitch is a romantic summer desert getaway (comment AMOR to book); commenters report an $800 two-night minimum, no pets allowed, and that it's fully booked through the summer — one calling it proposal-worthy.

reels.title: 10 favorite sandwiches in L.A.
reels.summary: Libby and Ryan Lamont rank their 10 favorite sandwiches in L.A. after trying over 100 in the past year. In listicle style they hold each sandwich up, cut it in half to show the inside, and give the sandwich name, restaurant, and their verdict — shot casually at home with clear enthusiasm for the subject.

reels.title: Build a consistent AI photo style with one master prompt
reels.summary: Andries Ohneisser teaches how to build a "master prompt" system so AI photos stop looking like AI — "wrong lighting, weak texture, zero rhythm" — and instead look like they came from the same shoot. The five elements: camera logic (vertical flash, harsh contrast, 1080x1350), deliberate perspective control, explicitly named surfaces and materials, real-world imperfections, and recurring quirky motifs. Think like a DOP, not a prompt spammer.

reels.title: Would you have walked out of this Galliano show?
reels.summary: maison_mathews pairs Jeremy Healy's narration with archival footage from John Galliano's Dior Haute Couture FW2000 show — a red fully-sculpted dress, white-painted faces with black masks and green fur collars, black corsets and red hats. Healy calls the deliberately unsettling soundscape — synthetic "stitch" noises, deep bass drops, and BDSM-style moaning — the show's most disturbing element, with comments comparing it to the Eyes Wide Shut soundtrack. The caption asks "Would you have walked out of this show?" — and there were documented walkouts.

reels.title: Luma Ray 2 animates a Midjourney V7 image
reels.summary: Evolving AI demos Luma Labs' Ray 2 camera feature applied to a Midjourney V7 image by @heydin.ai — "feels like it was filmed with real gear: drone, BOLT, motion and angles are spot on." The split-screen compares real camera footage with the AI equivalent across aerial shots, handheld, dolly zooms, and crane shots on cars, models, and people — pitching it as another powerful tool for AI filmmakers.

reels.title: Cristiano Ronaldo ab workout
reels.summary: Bernardo Rebeil's "Cristiano Ronaldo Ab Workout" is a comedy of contrast: a shirtless, muscular man breezes through leg lifts, heel touches, suitcase twists, elbow-to-knee crunches, and toe touches while the voiceover delivers exaggerated frustration and disbelief at the difficulty — "throwing himself up" by the end. Workout plans in his bio.

reels.title: Walter Molino: the illustrator who made the ordinary look extraordinary
