reels.summary: Cured spotlights Walter Molino (1915–1997), the Italian illustrator who "made the ordinary look extraordinary" — best known for his eye-catching La Domenica del Corriere covers painting disasters, daring rescues, and even futuristic inventions, "like a movie frozen in time, full of action, movement, and emotion." The reel pairs his unsettling illustrations (a woman wielding roses like a weapon against a man, a tiger menacing a baby in a crib) with dramatic spoken-word narration, all dark humor and dread.

reels.title: LA hidden gems: historic homes & gardens
reels.summary: Remy Solomon shares her favorite LA historic home tours: the Schindler House (accessible, with rotating art exhibits), the Frederick R. Weisman House (a museum filled with art), the Neutra House (detailed design), the sprawling Virginia Robinson Gardens, and the Eames House — which she's been wanting to tour but finds cost-prohibitive. She also explains her hot take that she "kinda hates Frank Lloyd Wright": she used to work at a museum where she stared at his pieces for five hours at a time.

reels.title: 3-day NorCal road trip: Shasta, Burney Falls, Lassen (earlier cut)
reels.summary: An earlier cut of Tannya Cai's 3-day NorCal road trip itinerary, centered on the 1.5-mile Heart Lake hike: a night drive on a forest road, a first-person climb up a rocky trail, waiting for the fog to clear — then a breathtaking panoramic view of the heart-shaped lake with Mount Shasta behind it. "Best ROI hike in California": the effort and patience are rewarded with an unforgettable view.
reels.creator_name: Tannya Cai | adventure • travel • photography • drone

reels.title: Build Wars: Lovable AI vs Webflow in a 45-min landing page race
reels.summary: Tommy Geoco recaps Build Wars — a livestream that drew 40,000 viewers after a "Webflow is dead" tweet turned into a 45-minute design race: Lovable.dev vs Webflow, no prep, real stakes. Design veteran Brett (DesignJoy, on Webflow) faced marketer Henrik (on Lovable) building a Pulse Robotics landing page with two interactions from provided assets. Henrik produced a slick animated robot hero in 10 minutes, but Brett's slower, more consistent build won the judges' unanimous vote — proving Webflow isn't dead. The event racked up over a million social interactions and nearly $200k in bets; the narrator asks who should compete next.

reels.title: (His)story
reels.summary: London B presents a curated list of music album covers, primarily from blues and rock artists: a subject sits on a ladder in a room with a guitar, holding up a digital interface that displays the covers one by one. A slow, soulful song with a narrative voiceover sets a pensive, reflective mood — a personal collection shared as a piece of music history. Caption: "(His)story."

reels.title: 'Myths Unveiled': Eyes Wide Shut conspiracy claims
reels.summary: Malik Bade pitches his book series The Matrix & The Forbidden Knowledge (Parts 1–5) through an Eyes Wide Shut conspiracy lens: split-screen imagery of Kubrick's ritualistic gatherings, grand castles, and masks paired with a distorted, muffled voiceover criticizing Kubrick. "Myths Unveiled" is billed as "the only critical work of our time," revealing "the final revelation of what our world has still to experience" — with Eyes Wide Shut framed as Kubrick's final statement on the bizarre perversions of the wealthy elite.

reels.title: Comorin Gurgaon: mutton seekh kebab & Champaran mutton
reels.summary: Karan Marwah revisits Comorin in Gurugram, ranked 79th on Asia's 50 Best Restaurants: the signature mutton seekh kebab — "melt-in-mouth" and spicy, served in a small skillet with melted hot butter and Kashmiri-bakery-inspired bread — plus Champaran mutton, prawn starters, and his favorite sweet corn khichdi. Beyond the food, he credits the whole package: the ambiance and a "crazy good" cocktail programme, keeping it one of his favorites in Gurgaon.

reels.title: 2025 rebrand roundup: OpenAI, Plaid, Frame
reels.summary: Tommy Geoco rounds up early-2025 rebrands, 49 days in: OpenAI's rebrand (praised for ASMR-like sound design and UI, dinged for its "model menu"), Plaid "going unnecessarily hard" with boldness for a finance company, and Frame's motion system — an example of a "small addition" to a design system that "makes me question my life choices." Dropbox's brand site and CopyAI's logo presentation get honorable mentions. The caption asks: what's your favorite rebrand so far?

reels.title: Verde Canyon Railroad: Sedona's mini Grand Canyon by train
reels.summary: Nicole Pang promotes the Verde Canyon Railroad — "Sedona's mini Grand Canyon by train": a vintage train winding through a narrow canyon and over a large metal bridge, with an open-air deck offering 360-degree views and a luxe interior of leather couches and wooden accents. Tickets start at $149 for the 4-hour ride, including snacks and a champagne toast. Comment "train" and she'll send the booking link plus her Sedona Guide.
reels.creator_name: Nicole Pang 🌵 USA Travel + Solo Hiking + Vanlife

reels.title: $120K Kaggle market forecasting competition
reels.summary: Nick Amato flags a $120,000 Kaggle competition with six months remaining: Jane Street Real-Time Market Data Forecasting. The challenge is to build a model in Python or R predicting market behavior from anonymized data — narrowing down features through exploratory data analysis. He walks through the leaderboard and prize breakdown, encouraging data scientists to enter solo or as a team on kaggle.com.

reels.title: IKEA BESTÅ TV bench setup tour
reels.summary: Paulien De Clercq answers her most-asked question — where the TV bench came from — with a setup tour of the IKEA BESTÅ system. She notes it's an advertisement for @ikeabelgium, but she bought the bench "wayyyy before" starting Instagram. Tags: #ikea #tvbench #interior #bookshelf #homedecor #apartmenttherapy.

reels.title: 3 tools for discovering unique fonts
reels.summary: Daniil of filatov.design shares three tools for discovering free fonts: Free Faces Gallery, a curated collection of high-quality free fonts; Fontshare, with a wide range of modern typefaces; and Uncut, a free open-source typeface catalogue — all free to download and use. Comment "Fonts" and he'll send his curated pack of 50 unique fonts, from graffiti to elegant styles.

reels.title: The Toolbox: curated creative tools for junior designers
reels.summary: Jason Murray shares TheToolbox.art — his curated collection of tools and resources for junior creatives, "exactly what I wish I had when I was a junior creative." The free site (plus a free PDF) organizes resources in a clear grid: Visual Reference, Stock, Mockups, Free Fonts, and a "Who to Follow" section. Comment "TOOLBOX" and he'll DM the link — no gatekeeping.

reels.title: 3-day LA itinerary: Venice, Westwood, DTLA
reels.summary: Drew Tillman lays out a 3-day LA itinerary by neighborhood. Day 1, the West Side: a breakfast burrito at Society Kitchen, the Anima Mundi apothecary in Venice, a walk through the Venice Canals, a pottery class at Still Life Studios, sunset on the beach, dinner at Fia, and a non-alcoholic kava nightcap at Kavahana. Day 2, Westwood: the Getty Center, Broxton Brewery, The Breathing Room wellness, the Mathias Botanical Garden, and dinner at Violet Bistro. Day 3, DTLA: coffee at Aquarala in the historic Cal Edison building, The Broad, happy-hour dinner at Perch with a rooftop view, and drinks at Level 8 (eight bars and restaurants).

reels.title: Matty's Patty's Burger Club opens first US location in Costa Mesa
reels.summary: Lane Stone covers the opening of Matty Matheson's first US Matty's Patty's Burger Club, in Costa Mesa on Newport Blvd by 17th — in the old late-night donut shop space. She orders the double patty with Matty's Patty's Sauce, fries, and poutine, declaring her love for a good smash burger and passing on the word that the chili fries are "💣."

reels.title: Browser-based animation tool — forget After Effects?
reels.summary: Saptarshi Prakash pitches Modyfi (modyfi.com) — "FORGET After Effects!" It's a browser-based tool for realistic dynamic animations with a huge set of customizable effects and a Figma-like interface, free to use. The reel is day 101 of his design-resource series; he urges viewers to watch to the end and follow for more.

reels.title: Kaiber Superstudio: a Figma-like canvas for generative AI
reels.summary: Kallaway introduces Kaiber's Superstudio — "Figma for generative AI": an infinite drag-and-drop canvas where modules and connectors chain different AI models (Flux, image restylers, Luma video) into visual workflows. The demo shows a high-cost animated logo video built entirely in the platform, arguing users can "fractionally tap into different AI models" instead of juggling dozens of subscriptions — "Kaiber has entered the chat."

reels.title: Maneken: premium drag-and-drop mockups in the browser
reels.summary: Jason Murray recommends maneken.app — "super premium" drag-and-drop mockups entirely in the browser, no Photoshop files or smart objects needed. The library spans tote bags, billboards, storefront signs, t-shirts, hats, phone and laptop screens, coffee cups, and building banners: drop in images or video, colors auto-fill, and export to exact specs. Free for a lot of features with a Pro plan for everything — and he notes the video is not sponsored.

reels.title: Mid-century loft: daylight vs nighttime
reels.summary: Eloise Preen tours her mid-century loft in daylight and at night: a living area with a green velvet sofa, glass coffee table, and orange floor lamp; a home office with an iMac; a bedroom with a "LIFE IS VERY GOOD" poster and orange velvet chair; a kitchen with a TV reading "FLUMNATION"; and a terrace with city lights beyond. Daytime is all natural sunlight; nighttime runs on warm orange lighting — the transformation set to a smooth R&B track, "Vibes on light."

reels.title: Farm to Smash: $7.99 smash burgers in Escondido
reels.summary: Judy Ha-Guevarra spotlights Farm to Smash in Escondido: fresh-cut fries cooked in beef tallow, fresh-ground patties smashed to perfection every time, preservative-free buns from a local bakery, and house-made mayo with avocado oil — a single burger starts at just $7.99. They also make premium ice cream shakes.

reels.title: Moyai emoji reel
reels.summary: A one-panel meme: a static Moai statue on Easter Island with overlaid text — "Yall better not be stoned when I get there" and "Us when you get here:" — a playful warning about the creator's arrival. The humor is the contrast between the ancient, solemn statues and the casual modern text. Caption: 🗿.

reels.title: Favorite men's graphic tees
reels.summary: Stylist Alexandra Ballard shares her favorite men's graphic tees right now, browsing a catalog on screen spanning Nude Project, Scuffers, Motel Margarita, Malbon Golf, Abercrombie, Nike, Air Jordan, Adidas, Carhartt WIP, About Blank, OnlyNYC, We Are The Peace, and Revolve. Comments debate the $50–$70 price points, suggest thrift-store alternatives like L-train Vintage and Buffalo Exchange in New York, and note she posted a link to an affordable version.

reels.title: 5 tips for luxury hotel-style curtains
reels.summary: Furniture Factoree gives five tips for 5-star-hotel curtains at home: (1) hang them as tall as possible — floor-to-ceiling for a grand feel; (2) ditch bulky rods for sleek ceiling-mounted curtain channels; (3) cut a pelmet/niche into a false ceiling to hide the channel; (4) choose your pleats — goblet, eyelet, or his favorite, the pinch pleat; (5) layer a blackout curtain for privacy with a sheer for light. Pro tip: leave a small gap at the floor for easier cleaning.

reels.title: The Lookout at Lake Poway Café: breakfast with a view
reels.summary: Ro visits The Lookout at Lake Poway Café — formerly Lake Poway Café — now with an espresso bar, hot food, beer & wine, and ice cream, all with the "best view in town" over the lake. It's pitched as the perfect post-hike (or post-fishing, post-duck-feeding) retreat after tackling the 3-mile loop. The aesthetic reel pairs waffles, avocado toast, coffee, and a green smoothie with ducks on the lake — under a melancholic electronic track for a slightly ironic, memorable effect.

reels.title: Girl & boy mid-century loft tour
reels.summary: Eloise Preen tours a stylish loft with calm, aesthetic footage — living room with a big potted plant, dining area with an orange paper lantern, balcony with a city view. The playful layer is the audio: the viral "Have you ever been in love?" / "Absolutely." meme clip, giving the home tour an internet-savvy, humorous finish. Caption: "girl & boy loft 🛋️☕️🌞."

reels.title: Free AI training newsletter — comment 'BAAM'
reels.summary: Kushank Aggarwal demos a two-step AI productivity hack: scrape Instagram data (post URLs, likes, comments) with Apify, then upload it to Julius AI for correlation analysis — producing a bar chart of average video views per posting hour to find the optimal posting time. Comment "BAAM" for his free AI training newsletter.

reels.title: Men's style staples (sneakers)
reels.summary: Madison Gustini breaks down the "4 types of shoes every man needs": fashion sneakers (Adidas, Oliver Cabell, Puma, New Balance, Converse), all-leather white sneakers for business casual, loafers (G.H. Bass, Banana Republic, Suitsupply), and boots — especially Chelsea boots in pointed and square toes. She walks through pricing, materials, and why each earns a spot in a versatile wardrobe.

reels.title: Fairmont Banff: Canada's iconic castle hotel
reels.summary: Braden Stanley tours the Fairmont Banff Springs — "one of the most famous hotels in Canada" — the castle-style hotel built in 1888 and renovated since. Highlights: the Rundle Bar with its hidden door, the spa's indoor mineral pool and waterfall pools, the Cascade Ballroom, afternoon tea with mountain views, the ice skating rink, and fire pits. Tag someone you'd stay here with.

reels.title: What's your favorite thriller ever?
reels.summary: Liam Saul asks "What's your favorite thriller ever?" with a video of Sébastien Stan speaking to camera and a caption stacking recent psychological thrillers: Speak No Evil, Blink Twice, A Different Man, The Substance, I Saw The TV Glow, It's What's Inside, Bird, Heretic, and The Wasp. Comments add context: Speak No Evil exists as a 2022 Danish original and a 2024 American remake; I Saw The TV Glow is a trans-experience horror film; A Different Man is body horror; The Substance is philosophical; Bird (2024) stars Adam Pearson — with several titles streaming on MAX, Prime Video, or Netflix.

reels.title: Fifty Shades relatable meme
reels.summary: A two-panel meme from mostly.randomness: top, Dakota Johnson smiling and waving in an orange shawl with a tilak — "The two personalities that guys want in a girl"; bottom, a dim close-up of her as Anastasia Steele with a thin black cord around her neck, nodding to Fifty Shades' BDSM themes. Comments play the duality — "forgive me father / punish me daddy," "pray vs grey," "din me pray raat me grey" — celebrating (and some criticizing) the holy-vs-sin framing of male expectations.

reels.title: Larry Clark's Kids (1995): a raw portrait of '90s youth
reels.summary: The Better Cinema pairs an earnest caption about Larry Clark's Kids (1995) — "a raw, unflinching portrait of youth culture in the '90s," following a day in the lives of reckless New York teens through youthful impulsivity, substance abuse, and violence — with a meme video: two young men casually walking, one pretending to drink from a trophy, under the text "A FILM THAT TRAUMATIZED AN ENTIRE GENERATION" and somber ambient music. The ironic contrast is the joke: exaggerated meme-format disdain for the film.

reels.title: Simple trick for location tracking
reels.summary: TRUETECH100 demos a purported "simple trick" for location tracking: generating a link via a URL shortener (associated with IP-logger services) and sending it to a target, so clicking it captures their location — shown targeting mobile devices, with a person in a dark blue hoodie operating a black Lenovo laptop at a desk. The video shows little procedural detail beyond the link generation, and the comments turn sarcastic, repeatedly mocking the method's inaccuracy.

reels.title: Cardi B performs 'Wanna Be' remix verse in Miami
reels.summary: A Cardi B fan account posts her performing her verse from the "Wanna Be" remix at E11EVEN nightclub in Miami for New Year's — in a black lace bodysuit and green velvet skirt, engaging the crowd under blue and white spotlights. Video credit: @11miami.

reels.title: Day 13: YouTube videos to turn you into a polymath
reels.summary: Day 13 of Project Polymath's series of YouTube videos "that'll turn you into a Polymath": today's share is "Noam Chomsky — Manufacturing Consent" from the channel Chomsky's Philosophy, with the comment "If you don't have a seat at the table, you are probably on the menu." Check "Brain fertilizer" and "Novel nest" for deeper insights.

reels.title: AI is screening your job application — this guy wants to help
reels.summary: Christopher Wink (via @technical_ly) spotlights David Mosteller, a laid-off React developer who struggled to get applications past AI-powered Applicant Tracking Systems. Mosteller built a tool that analyzes your resume and flags what's getting it rejected by AI screening. He frames it in an "arms race" — one-click applications pushed employers to automated blocking — and argues his tool is a step toward making hiring more humane.

reels.title: Ghalib Kebab Corner, Nizamuddin: Delhi's underrated kebab gem
reels.summary: mahika refuses to gatekeep Ghalib Kebab Corner in Nizamuddin — "NO THIS IS NOT IN OLD DELHI" — calling the old, underrated spot "literally heaven" for Mughlai food. Highlights: melt-in-the-mouth galouti kebabs, juicy mutton and chicken seekh kebabs, plus nihari, kormas, and kamri roti, all mouth-watering and affordable (commenters cite kebabs around ₹15 and kamri roti ₹5). Comments confirm the shami kebab, butter chicken, and biryani, with some noting a recent ownership change.

reels.title: It actually works — rethinking modern kids' shows
reels.summary: Nika Diwa shares a parenting hack that "actually works": swapping overstimulating modern kids' shows for classic Japanese anime — here, Kiki's Delivery Service — to regulate her toddler's behavior. The cozy living-room scene shows the calm toddler under a blanket and the whole family, dad included, watching together to the anime's gentle, nostalgic music. She's now "thinking of cutting modern kids shows altogether."

reels.title: Kakori kebab (₹479) at Al Kausar, Vasant Vihar
reels.summary: Food vlogger india spotlights the Kakori Kebab (₹479) at Al Kausar in Vasant Vihar (Vasant Place Market, 30, near Malai Temple, Sector 6, R.K. Puram, New Delhi). The nighttime footage shows the neon-lit storefront, chefs preparing flatbreads and spiced kebabs, and close-ups of biryani and fried snacks — leaning on the brand's "king of kakori kebabs since 1896" reputation. Warm, inviting, and designed to sell Al Kausar as a must-visit for authentic Indian cuisine.

reels.title: Unlimited OCR: free AI model reads 100-page PDFs in one shot
reels.summary: Ikjot Juneja spotlights Baidu's open-source "Unlimited OCR," a 3-billion-parameter model from China that reads entire 100-page PDFs in a single pass instead of chopping documents page-by-page and losing context. The GitHub repo (baidu/Unlimited-OCR) demos converting a 40-page contract into clean structured markdown and preserving a Q3 financial report's tables, charts, formulas, headings, and reading order. He claims it kills the messy PDF-preprocessing stack for RAG pipelines and document search, runs locally so documents never leave your system, and is MIT-licensed and free for commercial use. Comment 'OCR' to get the link.

reels.title: Directed shots for filming yourself driving
reels.summary: Alexander Sworik demos seven labeled cinematic shots for filming yourself driving, "but directed": shot_001 low-angle approach of a man walking to a vintage blue Chevy truck, shot_002 medium shot entering the truck, shot_003 through-the-window entry, shot_004 ignition insert of the hand turning the key, shot_005 front-windshield start, shot_006 medium-wide drive away, and shot_007 a mounted side profile of the driver. Set on a rural gravel road at golden hour with 'Fortunate Son' by Creedence Clearwater Revival playing, the tutorial teaches composition and lighting for automotive content.

reels.title: Basic UI components that make or break a project
reels.summary: Alex Harmon (@avoshuu) shares three foundational UI design tips: use a proper icon library instead of low-quality defaults — he recommends Reicon, an open-source library with thousands of icons; install an animation library like GSAP or Framer Motion to make interfaces feel premium, showing animated slides and hover effects; and mind rounded corners and spacing for a polished look. Screen recordings show the Reicon site, its icon grid, and the GSAP homepage. Caption invites viewers to comment to join a builder community.

reels.title: Free Claude skill turns brands into animated 3D scrolling sites
reels.summary: Ali promotes 'Scroll World,' a free open-source Claude skill that turns a brand description into an animated 3D scrolling website. The workflow: install the skill, describe the site, and it generates still images, converts them to video clips, and stitches them into a 'fly-through-the-world' scroll experience with smooth camera transitions — no designers or video editors needed. Demos show a boba tea scene, a luxury cliffside home interior at sunset, and a car on a highway. The repo has 3,500+ GitHub stars; comment 'SCROLL' to get the link.

reels.title: Storagemaxxing at home
reels.summary: Eric Luis presents five IKEA home updates for 'storagemaxxing': the white VARIERA bag dispenser mounted on a dresser to store toddler socks; the beige HUSBYÅn wall cabinet by a doorway for small items, decorated with magnets; the metal VARIERA pot lid organizer on a sideboard to display vinyl records in rotation; black MURVEL shoe organizers stacked on a wire rack to maximize vertical shoe storage; and KLYKET folding hooks drilled into an entryway wall for keys. Calm, aesthetic, dialogue-free home tour.

reels.title: OfficeCLI: AI agents control Word, Excel, PowerPoint in one line
reels.summary: OfficeCLI is a free, open-source tool that gives any AI agent full control over Word, Excel, and PowerPoint in one line of code, without Microsoft Office installed. Built for AI agents, it creates documents from scratch, reads text and formulas, edits styles and layouts, and renders files as images so the AI can see its work. Installation is a single command pasted into the agent's chat, and it's compatible with Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot. Comment 'OFFICE' to get the repo link.

reels.title: I asked Claude to find every photo of me on the internet
reels.summary: Maverick Maltin (@mavgpt) demonstrates using Claude to find every photo of yourself on the internet: upload a selfie, have Claude analyze your identifying features, connect Chrome via Connectors settings, then ask Claude to reverse-image-search across top tools and return links to every place you appear. Screen recordings show it returning Google Images results for 'Maverick + Maltin' across Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube, and TikTok — results he calls 'honestly terrifying.' A bonus prompt generates custom privacy removal request letters for each site. Comment 'Privacy' to get the prompts.

reels.title: $500K chip design licenses just went free (open-source tapeout)
reels.summary: Pranav explains how a UC San Diego project gives electrical engineering students free access to the RTL-to-GDS chip design flow that previously needed $500K-per-year Cadence or Synopsys licenses. Clone a repo, feed in Verilog, and it produces a fabrication-ready physical layout — the same flow has produced over 600 real chip tapeouts through Google's efabless shuttle program, i.e. actual silicon, not class projects. The only requirement is a supported PDK like Skywater130; OpenROAD handles placement, routing, and timing closure automatically. Comment 'TAPEOUT' for the setup DM.

reels.title: Welcome Kimi 3!
reels.summary: Adonis spotlights Kimi K3 as a cheaper alternative to Claude and ChatGPT, noting the distillation accusations against it (he likens it to copying homework). Its standout: #1 on the Frontend Code Arena leaderboard for frontend design. He cites a Max Weinbach tweet showing Kimi K3 recreating macOS 27 with Liquid Glass using just 60% of a $40 monthly plan, then demos it redesigning his own site adonisautomates.com — modern UI, statistics, and case studies he calls 80–90% of the way there and sellable for $1,000+. He used the free plan and discloses paid tiers may exist.
reels.creator_name: Adonis Cyril | AI in Real Estate

reels.title: Claude Code guides
reels.summary: Chase presents 'herdr,' an open-source 'agent multiplexer' he describes as 'tmux but for AI agents' — essential if you run Claude Code and Codex together or juggle multiple coding agents. Its interface monitors and controls multiple terminals with different agents in one place, separates them by spaces, and shows status indicators like working, idle, blocked, and complete. Closing herdr doesn't kill the agents: they persist as a server so work isn't lost. It's fast, lightweight, and runs on Windows and Mac. Comment 'agent' to get his Claude Code guides.

reels.title: High-protein butter garlic chicken (58g protein, 472 cal)
reels.summary: Chef and certified nutritionist Aathira Sethumadhavan (@aathirasethumadhavan) demos a creamy butter garlic chicken with 58g protein and 472 calories per serving (2 servings of 225g each). Cubed chicken breast is marinated in cornflour, baking soda, soy sauce, salt, and pepper, then pan-fried until golden; the same pan gets light butter, chopped garlic, soy sauce, chili flakes, and pepper, plus a smooth puree of high-protein paneer blended with hot water. The chicken goes back in, gets tossed with spring onion greens, and finished with lemon juice. One pan, no deep frying, browned outside and tender inside.

reels.title: Claude Code guides
reels.summary: Chase showcases 'Taste Skill — The Anti-Slop Frontend Framework for AI Agents,' the fastest-growing AI repo for better front-end design with Claude Code, with over 50,000 GitHub stars. The suite of skills targets 'AI slop' in web design with stronger layout, typography, and motion, and can hook into Claude Code's image-generation skills using GPT Images to improve frontends. He shows two example sites: a dark-themed 'Botanic Architecture' floral site and a light SaaS dashboard for 'Power Agency Growth Through Partners,' calling them a step above standard Claude Code output. Search 'Taste Skill' on GitHub; comment 'agent' for his Claude Code guides.

reels.title: Type a prompt, watch a real UI appear on a live canvas
reels.summary: OpenPencil is pitched as the world's first open-source AI-native vector design tool (GitHub: ZSeven-W/openpencil). Type a prompt and watch a real UI get drawn live on a canvas, auto-split into parts so multiple AI agents build sections in parallel like a small design team, with text edits updating the canvas instantly. It offers 50 built-in styles, integrates with Claude Code, Copilot, and Gemini CLI via MCP Server, runs on desktop or server, and exports real React or HTML code. Installs on macOS, Windows, Linux, and Docker. Follow gittrend.io for more open-source repos.

reels.title: Claude resources (CTA-only)
reels.summary: Brody (@brodyautomates) walks through Voicebox, an open-source AI voice studio that clones a voice from seconds of audio, generates speech, and dictates into any app via a hotkey — all running locally on your machine with no APIs. He compares it to paid ElevenLabs and Whisperflow, noting 23 supported languages, 33,000+ GitHub stars, and a '#1 Repository of the Day' badge. He demos the terminal install and says it replaces his two most-used subscribed tools. Comment 'Repo' for the GitHub link.

reels.title: AgentReach: one install gives AI agents 13 platforms, zero API fees
reels.summary: Unnati Tripathi (@aiwithunnati) covers Agent Reach, an open-source GitHub repo (Panniantong/Agent-Reach, 38,000 stars) that gives AI agents read-and-search access across 13 platforms — Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Instagram, LinkedIn, and more — without paid APIs. It performs unauthenticated reads, bypasses bot-blocking walls, pulls YouTube transcripts, works on sites that hard-block server IPs, and scrapes bot-resistant platforms. Demoed in Claude Code via a single pasted command, it can check Reddit, pull YouTube comments, or search Twitter reactions for any topic in real time. Free and open source; comment 'agent' for the DM link.

reels.title: Visualize user flows as storyboards with /visual-plan
reels.summary: Builder.io CEO Steve Sewell (@steve8708) demonstrates his favorite workflow tool: the /visual-plan command in Claude Code v2.1.191, which generates a 'Signup Flow Storyboard' from your codebase instead of single screenshots. The interactive canvas maps end-to-end paths — auth entry, email verify, org resolution, and app-specific onboarding for Mail and Calendar apps — and helped him spot unwanted steps, like an org input prompt he thought was automated. He comments directly on the storyboard to instruct the agent to fix the code. The skill is open source at github.com/BuilderIO/skills.

reels.title: The coolest campground in California no one talks about
reels.summary: The Gabbett family (@gabbettfamilytravels) calls Laguna Seca Recreation Area — yes, you can camp at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca — the coolest campground in California no one talks about. Their elevated campsite overlooks the racetrack, where cars race along the curves, with a metal fire ring and picnic table in the foreground and dry rolling hills behind. Located in Monterey County on California's Central Coast, minutes from downtown Monterey, Carmel, and Pebble Beach, it was a spontaneous trip they say is ideal for car-obsessed kids.

reels.title: The Coveys — wedding preview (2000s rom-com style)
reels.summary: A cinematic wedding preview for Gracie and Matthew ("The Coveys") with a warm, sun-drenched 2000s-rom-com aesthetic, shot by @jasonsfilmlab. It opens with daytime prep — candles and blue hydrangeas being placed, flowers arranged, a white embroidered dress adjusted on a wicker mannequin — then moves to an outdoor lakeside ceremony with mountains behind: the bride walks a grassy aisle in a strapless gown, vows under a rustic arch, the kiss, and the walk back to applause. Evening brings a field run, first dance at dusk, dancing under string lights, cake feeding, and a berry-topped dessert, set to upbeat folk-pop.

reels.title: AI/tech resource (CTA-only)
reels.summary: Ayush (@ashh.decodes) demos 'ian-xiaohei-illustrations,' a GitHub repo / Claude skill that turns text prompts into black-and-white illustrations in under a minute. He clones the repo, installs it in a coding agent, and prompts it to illustrate AI processing data — within seconds it produces a simple diagram of a character scanning raw documents into structured output. He says the illustrations make explaining any topic easy and shows how the same image can be animated into an explainer for B-roll in content. He's tested it for a few days and calls it seriously impressive; comment 'REPO' for the link.

reels.title: GitHub Spec Kit: vibe-coding just grew up (100K+ stars)
reels.summary: Yury (@yury.ai) introduces GitHub's Spec Kit: instead of handing Cursor a vague task and letting the AI guess, you write the spec first, then the AI builds the plan, breaks it into tasks, and writes the code last — mimicking a real engineer. The repo passed 111,000 stars with 9.8k forks and 585 watching, and it works with Claude Code, Cursor, and 30+ other agents. He frames it as vibe-coding growing up: spec-driven development for AI-assisted coding. Comment 'SPEC' for the link.

reels.title: Mehendi celebration decor stitched with tradition
reels.summary: A POV tour of an elaborate evening Mehendi at Taj Lalit Bagh, Udaipur, styled by @thecreativecompany_team: walls draped in patchwork textiles, pyramids of woven baskets filled with marigolds and colored powders, fresh flower centerpieces in pink, orange, and yellow, low wooden seating with patterned cushions, a canopy of hanging fabrics, painted stools, terracotta pots, decorative wall plates, and a stage backdrop of circular floral arrangements. Set to a cheerful Hindi folk song. Dream team: design by @thecreativecompany_team, planning by @eventweaversindia, florals by @studiogul.in, venue @tajlalitbagh.

reels.title: Raincoat (2004): Rituparno Ghosh's melancholic tale of lost love
reels.summary: A clip from Rituparno Ghosh's 2004 film Raincoat, starring Ajay Devgn and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan: two former lovers reunite on a gloomy, rain-drenched afternoon in Kolkata, in a dimly lit room, over dialogue about a 'candlelight lunch' — he mentions skipping daytime meals and chewing gutka to avoid hunger. Stripped of typical Bollywood melodrama, the film unfolds almost entirely in that single room, relying on poignant dialogue and subtle expressions, in this melancholic adaptation of O. Henry's 'The Gift of the Magi.' The repost by @theviralvadapav suggests Devgn's performance feels like genuine emotion, not acting.

reels.title: Chutney recipe
reels.summary: A handwritten note titled '4 Types of Green Chutney' on a wooden surface lists four recipes with measurements: Sandwich Chutney, Dhaniya-Pudina, Coconut Green Chutney, and Dahi Wali Chutney — each with bullet-point ingredients and a photo of the corresponding chutney showing color variation from dark to light green. Set to an upbeat traditional Indian instrumental (shehnai-like wind instrument over rhythmic accompaniment), no spoken dialogue. A simple, educational home-cooking share from @dr.foodiephysiosurati.

reels.title: Idea to functioning iOS app in minutes (vibe coding)
reels.summary: Joaquin Fernandez (@kiksvibecodes) counts down the 'Top 5 Websites for Vibe Coders (Niche Edition)': #5 Aceterinity UI — animated React components to make apps look professionally built; #4 Refero Styles — pulls design DNA from top websites into one file for AI to read; #3 Mobbin — a searchable catalog of every screen from major apps to hand to AI; #2 Godly — a live gallery of the internet's best websites, worth browsing 10 minutes before building to raise taste; #1 10x — takes an app idea and generates a native iOS app with real SwiftUI code and App Store assets in minutes, no coding experience needed.

reels.title: Kofto ka salan — food I grew up with, ep. 9
reels.summary: Noor (@noor.baqtiar) makes kofta ka salan, episode 9 of 'The Food I Grew Up With.' The kofte: 500g ground meat seasoned with salt, turmeric, red chilli, green chillies, cilantro, mint, besan, and ginger-garlic paste, processed smooth and shallow-fried golden. The signature Hyderabadi masala: toasted peanuts, desiccated coconut, poppy seeds, sliced onion, almonds, and cashews blended with 250g yogurt. For the salan, whole spices (shah zeera, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon) bloom in hot oil with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli, and onions; the masala is roasted until oil separates, water is added and simmered under a lid, then cilantro, mint, green chillies, and garam masala are folded in before the kofte finish simmering in the gravy.

reels.title: Website/design resource (CTA-only)
reels.summary: Ayush (@ashh.decodes) demos getdesign.md, a site offering 'production-grade DESIGN.md analysis' built from iconic websites like Apple, Airbnb, and Figma. He scrolls through 100+ analyzed brands (including BMW M) and shows what each DESIGN.md file contains: exact color palettes, typography systems, buttons, cards, spacing layouts, and other UI elements. Download a file, drop it into Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, or another AI IDE, and the AI recreates fonts, colors, buttons, and spacing to match the brand. Hundreds of ready-made files are available for a few bucks each. Comment 'design' for the link.

reels.title: Sites I steal aesthetics from, part 5
reels.summary: Waviboy (@bywaviboy) shares part 5 of his series, '3 sites I steal every aesthetic from': The Brand Identity (T-BI) — the best branding on earth, updated daily, screenshot and feed to ChatGPT; Eye on Design — a full taste education on why design works; and Colossal — contemporary art unrelated to advertising for finding a 'vibe' before prompting AI. His tip: feed references into an LLM like Claude or Gemini, ask for a visual breakdown, and build a keyword library per aesthetic for your prompts. Comment 'STEAL' to get all three sites by DM.

reels.title: The most GOATed game of our childhood
reels.summary: A theatrical comedy skit by @dasoham_ paying tribute to Project I.G.I. as the most GOATed game of childhood. One actor plays two characters: an older version in bed with glasses and a nasal cannula, dramatically narrating his 2010 first mission — a helicopter insertion into a Russian base with tight security, dying 47 times before succeeding: killing guards, stealing the Dragunov sniper rifle, destroying a watchtower, and stealing a truck — intercut with actual I.G.I. gameplay footage showing the dated graphics and config screens. The younger version closes with 'Los Santos' and a 'TO BE CONTINUED' card, teasing a series on classic games.

reels.title: The viral 2011 'Boogity boogity boogity, amen' NASCAR prayer
reels.summary: The legendary 2011 NASCAR prayer: at Nashville Superspeedway, Pastor Joe Nelms delivers the pre-race invocation thanking God for 'mighty machines' — Ford, Dodge, Toyota, Roush Yates, Roush Fenway, GM, Sunoco fuel, Goodyear tires, and the RO7 engine — plus his 'smoking hot wife Lisa' and their children Eli and Emma, closing with Darrell Waltrip's 'Boogity, boogity, boogity, amen.' The video intercuts drivers and crew (including Austin Dillon in a Rheem suit) with heads bowed on pit road. Reposted by @viraldowntown as 'The European mind cannot comprehend this' — a long-running meme of evangelical faith, American motorsports, and sponsor culture.

reels.title: Bahu Swagat: a Rajasthani-inspired bridal welcome in Jodhpur
reels.summary: Aash Studio's 'Leheriya Chowk' — a Bahu Swagat bridal welcome in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, built around Leheriya tie-dye fabrics in bright pink, yellow, and orange. The outdoor showcase cycles through a massive draped fabric canopy, oversized embellished umbrellas as sculptural focal points, a large hot-air-balloon structure with mirrors and tassels, marigold and sunflower florals, market-style corners with pottery and bangle-making, a block-printing stall, colorful low seating with patterned cushions, and bars decorated with hanging paper motifs. Set to traditional Indian devotional and folk chanting with rhythmic percussion.

reels.title: Clearing up fear around the new USCIS Adjustment of Status memo
reels.summary: Immigration attorney Rhoda Agyeman-Frimpong (@bethellawimmigration) addresses fear over the May 21, 2026 USCIS policy memo on Adjustment of Status. She clarifies AOS has NOT been eliminated, people are not being denied across the board, and the memo does not force everyone into consular processing — it simply restates long-standing law that AOS under INA Section 245 is discretionary relief, not guaranteed approval. In practice she predicts more RFEs, Notices of Intent to Deny, and heavier scrutiny of immigration history, unlawful presence, prior violations, fraud concerns, and criminal issues. USCIS can't override statute by memo; careful preparation, strong documentation, consistency, and credibility matter most. Consultations: Bethel Law Group, 508-439-4445. Informational, not legal advice.

reels.title: $1000 full outdoor kit that takes you almost anywhere
reels.summary: Jackson (@outdoorjackson) builds a 'high quality mid-range outfit' for under $1,000 in part 2 of his hiking-kit series: Danish Endurance Core base layer set ($109); pants — Mountain Hardwear Rambler Convertible ($97 on sale), Kuhl Renegade Rock ($109), or Peak Performance cargo ($150); mid-layers — Mountain Equipment Jorasses Lite fleece ($150), Outdoor Research Vesper insulated jacket ($168 on sale), or a Polartec Alpha piece under $100 (Senchi, Burgeon, Viapex, LEVE, Squak); Patagonia Torrentshell 3L shell ($189); Osprey Hikelite 28L backpack ($165); and ~$200 budgeted for shoes bought to fit locally. Follow for part 3 on premium kits.

reels.title: Crimson Gold: the film starring a real-life pizza delivery man
reels.summary: Lillith spotlights Jafar Panahi's 2003 Iranian film Crimson Gold, co-written by Abbas Kiarostami — framed not as a heist movie but 'a 90-minute panic attack about being poor.' The lead is Hossain Emadeddin, a real-life Tehran pizza delivery man living with paranoid schizophrenia, who was given no traditional script: Panahi placed him in real luxury penthouses and upscale jewelry stores to capture his raw, genuine reactions to an elite world that ignored him. The result is a slow-burning, deeply uncomfortable study of class warfare considered too dark for Iranian audiences. Social realism about class disparity, not a lighthearted crime thriller.

reels.title: The mobility routine you should already be doing
reels.summary: Fitness coach Trevor Shan (@trevorsinstinct) demos a 5-minute, 10-move morning mobility routine from his Sacramento living room, 30 seconds per movement: jumping twists to get blood pumping, arm circles for shoulder range of motion, 'aura farmers' to open the arms and thoracic spine, McGregor-style clears, body waves to wake the spine, yogi lunges for hip/core balance, Cossack squats for lower-body mobilization, pump stretch/human cat stretch, bridges for back and shoulders, and lying windshield wipers to reset the spine. Benefits he cites: rehydrating fascia, nervous system activation, and being 'ready for life.' Save the routine if you follow him.

reels.title: Vercel Agent Browsers: a dedicated browser session for Claude
reels.summary: AI Honeycove (@ai.honeycove) explains Vercel's Agent Browsers (github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser), which gives Claude its own dedicated browser session to navigate the web, click buttons, and extract content without burning Claude tokens. Unlike Claude for Chrome or Playwright MCP — which he says waste tokens on full screenshots and giant tool definitions — Agent Browsers feeds Claude a clean accessibility (A11Y) tree with smart references (@E1, @E2), consuming 15x fewer tokens per screenshot: 'NO TOKEN BURN,' 'ZERO SCREENSHOTS,' 'OWN SESSION.' He frames it as making browser automation CLI practical for AI agents — tasks that once exhausted context windows now barely register.

reels.title: Playbook (CTA-only)
reels.summary: Zach Chang (@zchangd) introduces Anthropic's newly released 'Founder's Playbook: Building an AI-Native Startup,' pitched as a survival resource for AI agency owners instead of being displaced by new updates. Screen recordings of the playbook PDF show the table of contents and pages on MVP stage, customer discovery, market research, outreach via Claude Codework, security reviews, and GTM. He frames it as a checklist for how an AI agency can improve a business's leverage using Claude and agentic AI — much of it may already be known, but it works as a sanity check. It's free; comment 'checklist' to get it.

reels.title: Getting well-read in 2026
reels.summary: Nathan (@nathislate) recommends three books you can finish in an afternoon instead of doomscrolling: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy by Douglas Adams — absurdist humor that is genuinely philosophical about how small and meaningless everything is, yet comforting; The Prince by Niccolò Machiavelli — a cheat code to how power works in business and relationships, possibly toxic but genuinely insightful; and White Nights by Fyodor Dostoevsky — a genius portrait of a specific loneliness, feeling everything but unable to connect, a beautiful tragedy that makes you feel seen in an uncomfortable way.

reels.title: Alazayem in El Cajon: San Diego's OG Iraqi spot since 2013
reels.summary: Min & Chloe (@mealswithmin) visit Al Azayem in El Cajon — San Diego's OG Iraqi spot since 2013, a family-run restaurant at 550 E Main St (parking lot in back). Standouts: lamb shank with vermicelli rice, peas, and carrots where the meat falls off the bone; a mixed grill of chicken kebab and kofta over yellow rice; beef shawarma wraps with fries and yogurt sauce (praised for the sear); hummus topped with olives; and a tomato-based bean stew. They call the food phenomenal at a reasonable price, highlighting tenderness, seasoning, and homemade quality.

reels.title: Book recommendations: which ones should be added to the list?
reels.summary: Steven James Reese (@stevenjreese) delivers a monologue on the Southern Gothic novel genre — America's invention of humidity, decaying mansions, Spanish moss, and the legacy of slavery and violence beneath a polite surface, emerging after the Civil War to call out the South's self-justifying story through the grotesque. His three-book syllabus: William Faulkner's Absalom, Absalom! (1936) on Thomas Sutpen's plantation empire rising and collapsing across generations; Flannery O'Connor's Wise Blood (1952) on Hazel Motes founding a 'Church Without Christ'; and Toni Morrison's Beloved (1987) on an escaped enslaved woman haunted by the daughter she killed. His thesis: the house is haunted because the country is haunted — and the only way out is through the basement. Comment which books should be added.

reels.title: The KBBQ checklist: what every San Diego spot is missing
reels.summary: Min reviews DJK Korean BBQ in San Diego, calling it the most authentic KBBQ he's found and the one spot that passes his checklist: good-quality meat with good marinades, good banchan, solid sides (steamed egg, soybean stew, soups), and correct sauces — ssamjang, not sambal. Highlights: marbling 'kissed by the flame' over a real charcoal grill, banchan that tastes like 'someone's grandma made it' (bean sprouts, yukgaejang spicy soup), a ~20-year-old restaurant run by Korean people, a free self-serve ramen station with the AYCE deal, plus Terra beer and Jinro soju.

reels.title: Chill hip hop playlist: good views and good tunes
reels.summary: Baylee Lefton (@ayybaybay_radio) shares four picks from her 90s & 2000s hip-hop rotation, standing on a lakeshore: 'Africa Dream' by Reflection Eternal (Talib Kweli, Hi-Tek), 'Feel The Music' by Guru featuring Paul Ferguson and Baybe, 'Next Level' by Show & A.G., and 'Recollect' by eXample — calling one her favorite hip-hop album and inviting commenters to add their own. Ends with a graphic for her 'Chill hip hop' playlist, link in bio.

reels.title: 40 garlic clove chicken
reels.summary: Kelly Scott (@kellyscleankitchen) makes Poulet aux 40 gousses d'ail — 40-clove garlic chicken, a classic French dish she learned working at a French restaurant. Skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks are seasoned, dried, and seared golden; the peeled cloves from 4–5 heads of garlic go in with butter and fresh thyme, get sautéed briefly, then deglazed with white wine and chicken stock. Covered, the pot bakes at 350°F for 45 minutes; half the cooked garlic is blended into the broth to thicken it, and the tender chicken is served smothered in the rich garlic sauce. She says it's worth peeling 40 cloves; comment 'SUBSTACK' for her newsletter, 'recipe' for the full recipe.

reels.title: Powerful websites you should know (part 994): animated components
reels.summary: Tony Chen (@setupsai) spotlights anime.js in 'POWERFUL WEBSITES YOU SHOULD KNOW (PART 994)': an 'all-in-one animation engine' JavaScript library where you can find almost any animated component — timers, animations, buttons — all beautifully designed, with code you can copy instantly and no login required. The walkthrough of animejs.com highlights timelines, timers, WAAPI sync, layout settings, stagger grid parameters, and an easings editor with spring presets.

reels.title: Fern Canyon: the unreal hike in Redwood National Park
reels.summary: Carson and Melissa McCraw (@mccrawsonthemap) guide a visit to Fern Canyon in Redwood National and State Parks: pay the $12 day-use permit, drive the narrow unpaved dirt road past stream crossings and elk in a meadow, then hike about half a mile through lush forest to a narrow slot canyon with a shallow creek — walls completely covered in ferns rising 30–50 feet straight up, creating a prehistoric, otherworldly atmosphere (it was a filming location for a Jurassic Park movie). Peak season (May 15–Sept 15) requires an advance reservation; check the National Park website. Wet feet are inevitable but worth it.
reels.creator_name: Melissa McCraw and Carson McCraw | RV Life | US Travel

reels.title: Sandstone Canyon: sit this off-road trail out if you're claustrophobic
reels.summary: Daniel Mendenhall (@dans_offroad_odyssey) drives Sandstone Canyon in Anza-Borrego Desert State Park — warning the claustrophobic to sit it out. The first-person journey goes through a maze of towering 75-foot vertical light-colored sandstone walls: washboard, deep sand, and tight slot canyon, so aired-down tires and spatial awareness are must-haves. His rigs include a light green Jeep Wrangler Rubicon and a black Toyota 4Runner. Geology note: the walls formed 19 million years ago and are packed with fossilized seashells — you're literally driving through an ancient ocean.

reels.title: Badlands: Terrence Malick's outstanding debut
reels.summary: A video essay from 'Tales From The Road — Day 6' on Terrence Malick's 1973 debut Badlands: the 28-year-old director's road movie starring Martin Sheen as Kit and Sissy Spacek as Holly — naive drifter meets Holly in a dead-end town, a deadly confrontation shatters their innocent romance, and they flee as fugitives across empty highways and endless fields. The essay argues Malick turns a Bonnie-and-Clyde setup into something atypical: a strange liminality where freedom and captivity juxtapose, the vast open sky and road paradoxically feeling like a locked room — one of the greatest debuts in American cinema.

reels.title: 'Bring It On' — Organized Konfusion (underground rap)
reels.summary: 'Bring It On' by Organized Konfusion, from the album Stress: The Extinction Agenda. Ida B. (@slyida.b) pairs the underground rap track with a relaxed visual of a woman preparing coffee, with the energetic hip-hop — featuring Pharoahe Monch, Prince Po, and production from Rockwilder and Buckwild — playing throughout, creating a playful contrast between the assertive music and the everyday scene.

reels.title: My 3-week honeymoon: Japan, Bali, Singapore, London on points
reels.summary: Jared (@pointedbyjared) lays out his three-week honeymoon round-the-world trip (June into July: Japan → Bali → Singapore → London) — first class on Japan Airlines and Singapore Airlines, staying at Aman Tokyo, Gora Kadan Fuji, Hotel The Mitsui Kyoto, Mandapa, Raffles, and The Connaught — all booked with points, a trip that would have cost over $100,000 in cash. He calls it his 'crowning achievement' as a luxury travel enthusiast and shares tips on supercharging points accumulation to elevate your own travel.

reels.title: 3 apps to manage your homelab servers
reels.summary: Software/cloud engineer Mason McCall (@masonamccall) recommends the first three apps for a homelab, demoed on his compact server rack with purple LEDs: 1) Tailscale — the Zero Trust identity-based connectivity platform, a VPN replacement for secure remote access; 2) Glances — the cross-platform Python system monitoring tool (CPU, memory, network, disk I/O, container stats) currently running on his screen; 3) Nginx Proxy Manager — to expose services securely with free Let's Encrypt SSL. Together they give you remote access, troubleshooting visibility, and easy navigation between your apps.

reels.title: AI/GitHub free tricks (CTA-only)
reels.summary: Divyam Dawar (@aiwithdivyam) presents a Hindi-language tutorial on three free web tools for the GitHub repo 'alphaXiv/OpenResearch': GitDiagram.com — paste a GitHub URL and get a visual architecture diagram of the codebase; Gitingest.com — ingest the whole repo to display its directory structure and file contents; and GitReverse.com — generate a 'reverse engineered prompt' describing what the project does. Framed as 'Don't tell me you don't know this 🤯'; comment anything to get the tool links.

reels.title: GTA 6 trailer message for creatives: the time is now
reels.summary: A cinematic Las Vegas montage by Taylor Jones (@tjonesvisuals) riffing on the message at the end of Rockstar's GTA 6 trailer. Aerial night views of the Strip give way to a reflective voiceover over sunset silhouettes, rooftop gatherings, and concert crowds: 'these are your glory days,' 'the salad years' — enjoy this, because if right now was all there is, all the time, it would be perfect. A shout to 'THE LINK UP' gathering outside COFFEE ROASTERS, framed as a communal message to fellow creatives: the time is now.
reels.creator_name: Taylor テイ・ジョーンズ

reels.title: Who's ready to hike the Dolomites?
reels.summary: Park (@parkisup) rates his '10/10 Male Purchases (Gorpcore Edition)' ahead of hiking the Dolomites: an Arc'teryx shell jacket, Salomon trail shoes, Nike ACG pants, Oakley EV Radar Path sunglasses, Arc'teryx beanies, Patagonia Cinchilla fleece pieces, a sticker-covered Nalgene bottle, and an Osprey backpack — each rated a perfect purchase in a fast-paced split-screen montage with product photos and on-screen labels.

reels.title: How to get the rarest satchel in RDR2
reels.summary: Jaspreet Singh (@imjassee) explains how to craft the Legend of the East satchel — RDR2's rarest item — which lets you carry 99 of every item. Prerequisites: unlock all six other satchels by buying leather working tools, fully upgrading the provisions and medicine wagons, and donating five animals to Pearson. Crafting the six requires perfect pelts: six deer, two elk, one badger, one squirrel, one panther, one bison, one raccoon, one boar, one iguana, one beaver, and one rabbit. Then craft the Legend of the East itself with one perfect deer pelt, one perfect cougar pelt, and one perfect wolf pelt.

reels.title: 3 movies that inspired Red Dead Redemption
reels.summary: Austin DeShayes (@austindeshayes) recommends three movies that inspired Red Dead Redemption: The Wild Bunch (1969) by Sam Peckinpah — aging outlaws in 1913 facing a modernizing West, with slow-motion shootouts and morally gray areas Rockstar has cited as a major influence; Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid (1973), also Peckinpah, starring Kris Kristofferson and James Coburn as former friends on opposite sides of the law, with slow mournful pacing and a Bob Dylan soundtrack paralleling Red Dead's story; and Sergio Leone's Once Upon a Time in the West (1968) — the king of spaghetti westerns, with revenge, greed, and technology themes, wide shots and tight close-ups like game cutscenes, and an opening train-station sequence that could be pulled straight from Red Dead.

reels.title: This weekend in San Diego: Aug 28-30 events
reels.summary: Katie Lynne Sonksen (@katielynnestyle) rounds up San Diego events for Aug 28–30: the Ramona Rodeo (@theramonarodeo) Aug 28–29 at 7PM at Ramona Outdoor Community Center; Damn Am street skateboarding Aug 28–30 at LVLUP Park, Vista; Jackalope Art Fair Aug 29–30, 11am–6pm at NTC Park, Liberty Station; Pirates of the Caribbean with the San Diego Symphony Aug 28 at 7:30pm at The Shell; San Diego Wave FC Aug 28 at 7pm at Snapdragon Stadium; Aeromyth (Aerosmith cover band) Aug 28 at 6:30pm at The Magnolia; and Thee Sacred Souls Aug 28 at 7pm at Petco Park. (Note: no video description was available; summary based on the caption.)

reels.title: Scroll Craft: AI skill that builds websites that scroll like a movie
reels.summary: Github Signals (@githubsignals) covers Scroll Craft, an AI skill for coding assistants that builds websites where scrolling feels like a movie. Instead of generic layouts, it forces the AI to pick from eight distinct visual styles and invent a unique interaction for every page, and it checks its own work by taking screenshots as it scrolls to ensure the design actually looks good — the result being a premium web experience. (Note: no video description was available; summary based on the caption.)

reels.title: Marvel says you only need 14 movies + 1 show for Avengers: Doomsday
reels.summary: Alex Rabinowitz (@popculturebrain) breaks down the official watchlist Disney/Marvel posted for Avengers: Doomsday (in theaters December 18, 2026): 14 movies — X-Men, X2, Captain America: The First Avenger, The Avengers (2012), Infinity War, Endgame, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, Spider-Man: No Way Home, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, Captain America: Brave New World, Deadpool & Wolverine, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, Thunderbolts*, The Fantastic Four: First Steps — plus the TV series Loki (both seasons). He reads the list as signaling returns from the original X-Men, the new Fantastic Four, Shang-Chi, Shuri, Mbaku, and Namor, with multiverse-heavy stories (Doctor Strange 2, Loki, No Way Home) informing Doomsday's plot. Rewatch, y/n?

reels.title: Episode 4: finding crazy GitHub repositories
reels.summary: Nishant Tiwari (@yournishaant) presents episode 4 of 'Finding Crazy GitHub Repos' (in Hindi with English on-screen text): github.com/public-apis/public-apis, a 455.9K-star collection of thousands of free public APIs organized by category — weather data, movies & web series, crypto trading prices, news, cloud sharing APIs, open data including NASA, and finance — useful for building apps or projects that need APIs. Comment 'API' for the direct link.

reels.title: Open-source AI PowerPoint tool (free Gamma alternative)
reels.summary: Keeran Jagadesan (@keeran.ai) demos PPT Master, an open-source AI tool (v4.5.0, MIT license, 45.3k stars, '#3 Repository of the Day') that generates native PowerPoint decks from any document — the free alternative to Gamma's paid product. Upload your company's actual template so it learns fonts, colors, and layout, hand it a source doc (PDF, DOCX, webpage), and it structures the narrative and outputs a fully editable .pptx with real shapes, transitions, charts, and speaker notes — it can even read the notes aloud. The demo deck: a dark-themed presentation titled 'Building Effective Agents.' Runs in Claude Code or ChatGPT; comment 'slides' for the GitHub link.

reels.title: Pani puri hunt in San Diego leads to a great outdoor spot
reels.summary: Erika Renée (@itserikarenee) tours Indya, a new family-owned modern Indian restaurant in San Diego's Clairemont neighborhood near Clairemont Town Square: a colorful two-story exterior with floral murals, lanterns, and a blue elephant fountain; a bright dining room and covered patio with hanging umbrellas; fusion items like naan tacos, tandoori pizza, and butter chicken pizza alongside classics. The pani puri (gol guppa) — crispy shells with chickpeas and potatoes, poured with spiced mint water — gets called refreshing; the butter chicken pizza on a naan crust and a mango lassi with a heart design are also praised. Note the daily $7 Happy Hour (4–6pm) and Indian-inspired brunch.

reels.title: Converting documents to Markdown before feeding AI gets messy
reels.summary: Akash Ingole (@_aijuice) flags a common AI workflow problem: converting documents to Markdown before feeding them to AI gets messy — tables break, financial data loses structure, formatting goes weird. His fix: Firecrawl's open-source AnyDoc (powered by pdf-inspector), a Rust-based local parser converting 14 formats — Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, CSV, EPUB — into clean .md with no separate parsers or API keys. Positioned as infrastructure for RAG systems handling hundreds of financial documents; runs locally with consistent output. Comment 'ANYDOC' for the GitHub link.

reels.title: Watch The Fog of War with your dad
reels.summary: Seb (@movieswithseb) recommends Errol Morris's The Fog of War (96% / 93% on Rotten Tomatoes; 'A masterpiece!' — Roger Ebert; 'Brilliant!' — Michael Wilmington) as the documentary to watch with your dad. Built around Robert McNamara — who ran the Pentagon through most of the Vietnam War — sitting down to explain what happened: a media-trained but ultimately sad man, viewed on camera as a war criminal, whose decisions cost millions of lives, plus his earlier work optimizing the bombing of Japan in WWII. Cited: a Letterboxd review on the film detaching numbers from human devastation. Archival footage of military briefings, Lyndon Johnson, and wartime scenes plays behind him.

reels.title: Anydoc: the SOTA document parsing tool
reels.summary: Paras Madan (@parasmadan.in) demos Anydoc, Firecrawl's open-source (Rust-built) document parser announced by CTO Nicolas Camara: any document → clean Markdown for AI, running fully in the browser with no uploads. Screen recordings show DOCX, PowerPoint, Excel, and old .doc files parsed instantly; install commands for Node.js, Python, Rust, and Browser WebAssembly. Claims: 500 files in 1.7 seconds, 94/100 on a 14-format benchmark (median 4.4ms vs 50ms–1s+ for competitors like LibreOffice, Unstructured, Pandoc), all under 5ms. Privacy angle: the file never leaves your computer. It now powers Firecrawl's parsing product.

reels.title: Pantools
reels.summary: AI Boy (@aiboy.ai) showcases The Bézier Game (bezier.method.ac), which turns learning the pen tool into a game. Against a dark interface, the player traces outlined shapes with the pen tool — placing nodes and adjusting Bézier handles — progressing from a human head profile, a heart, and a perfect circle to a classic car silhouette, an airplane outline, and a paperclip; each successful trace lights the path in color. Toolbar options include Undo, Redo, Clear Stage, Snap to Angle, and Unlink Control Handles. The voiceover explains it starts with simple lines and circles and builds to complex shapes, so you master a genuinely useful design skill without realizing you're learning.

reels.title: Claude Code skills, workflows, and guides
reels.summary: Chase addresses a hard Claude Code limitation — it can't watch video — with the 'watch' skill from the open-source bradautomates/claude-video repo. Workflow: hand it a video URL or file, it downloads it, checks for captions or generates a transcript via yt-dlp and Whisper, extracts frames with FFmpeg, then gives both frames and transcript to Claude, which answers based on what's actually on screen and heard. A frame-budget system manages token costs with duration-based allocations and extraction modes (efficient, balanced, token-burner). He calls it clever functionality missing out of the box; comment 'agent' for his Claude skills, workflows, and guides.

reels.title: The Claude Code setup repo that fixes AI agent mistakes
reels.summary: Sumit Paul (@wdf_ai) shares the GitHub repo 'CLAUDE CODEX SETTINGS,' which he says changed his entire Claude Code setup. Opening with Andrej Karpathy's tweet criticizing AI models for wrong assumptions, unmanaged confusion, and overcomplicated code, he presents the repo as the fix: battle-tested hooks, skills, plugins, and sub-agents, plus 'Real Plugins for Real Stacks' (Python, React, Stripe, MongoDB, Cloudflare, etc.). It works across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. Installation commands are shown on screen. 'Must Have For Developers'; comment 'Link' for the DM.

reels.title: RDR2: free Dark Bay Turkoman horse in Chapter 3
reels.summary: J-rok (@j_rok_gaming) guides getting RDR2's Dark Bay Turkoman — maxed health, near-max speed, not skittish like Arabians, free and available early in Chapter 3 (unlike the expensive Rose Grey Bay Arabian). The exploit: bring plenty of horse food, play the 'Horse Flesh for Dinner' mission (Arthur, John, and Javier stealing horses from the Braithwaites) until a stallion escapes, ensure the temporary horse icon appears on the map, then lasso and lead the Dark Bay Turkoman to the stable without bonding actions to keep it. The footage shows lassoing the loose stallion, approaching rustlers, feeding, and riding it to the stable.

reels.title: 4 niche engineering tools that'll make you disgustingly good
reels.summary: Meris Veladzic (@meris.veladzic) demos four niche engineering tools, in increasing niche: LTSpice — simulates analog circuits in time and frequency domains, imports any model, used by virtually every electrical engineer; OpenRocket — build custom rocketry and simulate high-altitude flight trajectories before physical launch; OpenFOAM — the open-source standard for computational fluid dynamics, simulating complex aerodynamic airflow (flow around a cylinder and airfoil) without expensive software; and KLayout — a silicon layout tool for designing actual microchip photo masks down to the nanometer level from a PC, shown with GDSII views and 3D mask structures.

reels.title: Why Indian banks are suddenly chasing US dollars (NRI GIFT City play)
reels.summary: The Pulsefy Duo (@thepulsefyduo) explain why Indian banks are 'suddenly chasing the US dollar': the HSBC GIFT City FCNR deposit product for NRIs offers 19x leverage. Walkthrough: deposit $100,000 for 3–5 years earning 5.5% interest, while the bank lends 19x that ($1.9M) at 5.1% — so you control $2M, earning $110,000 interest annually while paying $96,900 in loan interest, netting $13,100 — a 13.1% return on the original $100,000, claimed with no forex loss since it's USD-denominated. Educational disclaimer, not sponsored; comment 'INFO' for details.

reels.title: Stop buying e-SIMs: use this travel benefit instead
reels.summary: Anisha (@level.up.with.anisha) on a Chase Sapphire Reserve perk: the Visa Infinite card includes a GigSky partnership giving complimentary international eSIM data. Process: download the GigSky app, go to Offers & Benefits, enter your Visa card details, and unlock the free plan — the Visa Benefits page confirms the 'GigSky Global Mobile Data Plan for Visa Infinite Cards' offering 3GB for 15 days, free, with 30% off additional plans. It's data-only (no calls/texts; maps and messaging fine), renewable yearly, works in nearly 175 countries, and each eligible Visa Infinite or Signature card gets its own allowance (Sapphire Preferred as Visa Signature gets 1GB). Stop buying e-SIMs.

reels.title: Arizona's secret roller coaster highway
reels.summary: Nicole Ford (@nicolefordphoto) showcases State Route 97 near Bagdad, Arizona — 'Arizona's Secret Roller Coaster Highway.' What looks like an ordinary 10-mile connector between US 93 and the Bagdad area delivers massive dips, steep inclines, and sharp curves that create a roller-coaster ride through rugged desert backcountry, on smooth black asphalt winding through arid hills dotted with saguaro cacti under a blue sky. First-person driving perspective with yellow curve warning signs; follow for more Arizona fun.

reels.title: 14 things you MUST grab in Emerald Ranch (RDR2)
reels.summary: Ardee Artoo (@ardeeartoo) runs a clean single route to grab 14 things at Emerald Ranch in RDR2, with in-game map pins: the Theobald Getzin cigarette card at the saloon; the Flop Hat under stolen hats; windmill loot (Chicago cigarette card, Valerian Root); Larned Sod's warped tree (jewelry, cash, gold pocket watch, Mittie Comstock card); the Moonshine Hat (rugged outlaw look); the Black Mangrove card under the bench at Emerald Station; the Goat Carriage card inside the barn; a Gold Wedding Ring from a Black Merino sheep northwest of the ranch; another Gold Ring from a sheep at Guthrie Farm's southern shed; the Scarecrow Hat in the cornfield; the George Dixie card inside a house; and at Osman's Grove east of the ranch, loot from a dead family — the Otis Miller Book, Fountain Pen, Mary Beth's request, and provisions. 14 items, one route.

reels.title: How to find this cave (location details)
reels.summary: Shades (@by.shades_) reveals Bidi The Arch — a dramatic natural sandstone arch with sweeping wave-like striated walls and a sandy floor — hiding just behind a Shell gas station at 1501 Coppermine Road, next to Highway 98 in Page, Arizona. Directions: park in the dirt lot on the right side of the station, go through the opening in the metal fence, and the arch is about 100 yards back. Set to 'A Horse with No Name'; the creator asks visitors to be respectful since it's not a protected national park — 'places like these exist just behind a regular gas station in Arizona.'

reels.title: Lucky People Center International (1998): the wildest pre-Y2K documentary
reels.summary: A clip from Lucky People Centre International (1998), directed by Swedish multimedia collective Erik Pauser & Johan Söderberg, who spent two years traveling through 20+ countries filming shamans, gurus, Maori warriors, Tokyo salarymen doing weekend noise art, Russian poets, and Tibetan lamas. The fast-paced pre-millennium montage has people worldwide stating their faith — an Orthodox priest, a Buddhist monk, a man of the Nation of Islam, 'I believe in Hanuman,' a Brazilian Candomblé practitioner's 'Yemanja,' a sadhu's 'Shankar,' images of Lucifer, Kali, Xango, Oxun, Sita, Bhagwan, Rama — over the refrain 'Seek, seek, keep on asking,' closing with a Native American elder: 'everybody has to respect one another's religion.' Set to ambient electronic music; the poster calls it the wildest pre-Y2K documentary.

reels.title: GSTACK: Garry Tan's open-source '23 roles in one' for solo founders
reels.summary: Brand Nat (@brand.nat) explains gstack, Garry Tan's (Y Combinator CEO) open-source project that turns Claude Code into a virtual one-person company with 23 AI specialist roles — 'just the engine' vs 'the whole car.' It orchestrates CEO, PM, Engineer, QA Tester, and Release Manager agents together, uses cross-modal evaluation where three different AIs review every output to catch errors permanently, and runs a 'Skillify Loop' meta-skill that extracts patterns from manual work into automatically created reusable skills — so the system compounds and improves over time. Compatible with 100+ AI agents; free and open source. Comment 'GSTACK' for the GitHub link by DM.

reels.title: Claude Code + Codex in a custom agent management system
reels.summary: James Goldbach (@agentic.james) shows Claude Code and Codex running together in his custom agent management system, which he calls a huge unlock. (Note: no video description was available; summary based on the caption.)

reels.title: Hyperspace Pods: pool laptops into one AI cluster
reels.summary: Prithvi Raj Agrawal (@prithvirajagarawal) introduces Hyperspace Pods by 360Labs.ai: a family, startup, or group of friends pools laptops and desktops into a single local AI supercomputer. Workflow: install the software, create a pod with CLI commands like 'hyperspace pod create,' invite members, and a mesh network shares GPU resources automatically. From the outside it's a clean OpenAI-compatible API — paste the key into Cursor or Claude Code and prompts stay local, traveling from the IDE to pod members' hardware with no cloud server, subscription, or data leaving the device. Contrasted with $500/month Pro and $1,999/month Max cloud AI plans, it runs on hardware you already own; local inference demoed with Qwen 3.5 32B and GLM-5 Turbo.

reels.title: Chicken Kali Mirch: the royal black-pepper classic
reels.summary: Chef Ajay Kumar (@swadishbyajaykumar) makes Chicken Kali Mirch, the North Indian royal-kitchen black pepper chicken curry — 'underrated but unforgettable,' warm, peppery, with a lingering silky finish. Boneless thighs are cut into pieces and marinated in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, black pepper, and salt (optional but enhancing). The aromatic base: whole spices (green and black cardamom, cinnamon, peppercorns) bloomed with cashews, onions, garlic, and chilies in oil without browning, simmered with water, whole spices removed, then blended smooth. The chicken is seared in butter, combined with the sauce for a slow simmer until tender, then enriched with heavy cream, freshly crushed black peppercorns, and kasoori methi for a luxurious, restaurant-quality curry. Serves 2–3 (400g chicken).

reels.title: Koi value thodi na apni ✨
reels.summary: A young man sits on a set of stairs with a pained expression and says, 'Iss se bahar jaye hum koi image thodi na image up krni hai abe bhen.' The reel then cuts through a series of images with text overlays — 'Ek Innocent Life jiyenge,' 'Image UP krni hai,' 'Koi Value Thodi na,' and 'Abe Bhen' — set to somber music. It's a Hindi-language desi meme about self-worth and performing for other people's approval, where the comedy comes from the grand, contemplative presentation of deliberately mundane lines. Caption is mostly hashtags; the joke lives in the visuals and the dialogue.

reels.title: Things You Should Never Search on YouTube 🤔
reels.summary: A young man with dark hair sits at a desk speaking into a white spherical microphone, playing the 'Things You Should Never Search' internet meme template. In a serious tone, he warns viewers about things they should never search for on YouTube, while the top half of the screen cycles through memes matching his words — a SpongeBob scene, a man in a white mask eating from a bowl, and a man in a white shirt and tie typing on a laptop. The humor comes from the contrast between his grave delivery and the absurd visuals. Caption: 'Things You Should Never Search on YouTube 🤔'.

reels.title: Literature That Encapsulates Philosophy
reels.summary: A relatable POV meme for book lovers: it opens with a man on fire under the text 'POV: Philosophy and literature' versus 'Me who never felt understood by the world.' It then cuts to classic books including 'The Stranger' by Albert Camus, 'Notes from Underground' by Fyodor Dostoevsky, and 'Musashi' by Eiji Yoshikawa, with a tense rumbling sound effect building throughout. The joke is the feeling of being overwhelmed by heavy intellectual literature while feeling deeply misunderstood. Caption: 'Literature that encapsulates philosophy is my favourite genre of literature.'

reels.title: Roshun (Garlic) Bharta — Must-Try Garlic Recipe
reels.summary: Vinita Rathee (@mygardenofrecipes) demonstrates Roshun Bharta, a Kolkata-style garlic mash, in a Hindi voiceover. She heats mustard oil in a pan, fries two dried red chilies, then thinly sliced onions until golden brown, then 20–25 whole peeled garlic cloves until lightly browned. Everything is transferred to a tray, crushed by hand with salt and chopped fresh coriander (dhaniya), formed into a ball, and served over a mound of white rice with a green chili on top and mustard oil drizzled over. Caption recipe lists: 20–25 garlic pods, 2 dried red chilies, 1 sliced onion, 1–2 tbsp mustard oil, 1 tsp salt, fresh dhaniya. Note: comments heavily dispute the 'Kolkata's famous' claim, with many Bengali commenters saying garlic bharta is actually Bangladeshi/rural Bengal rather than a Kolkata dish.

reels.title: Relationship Goals Hashtags Reel
reels.summary: A comedy meme mocking the idea that girlfriends become a 'little version' of their boyfriend. On-screen text reads 'Pov: Your girlfriend is now a little version of you since she has spent so much time with you,' then cuts between a man in matching tracksuits (blue Elyce '42', red, orange), a gold chain, and a ride on a bright red Honda motorcycle with a female passenger mirroring his outfit and accessories. The viral 'Yeah! Stick that in your pipe and smoke it!' audio underpins it all. The joke is a sarcastic jab at couples copying each other until they lose individuality. Hashtag-only caption about relationships.

reels.title: Drove 2 Hours for the Best Tacos in LA
reels.summary: Jack from Jack's Dining Room (@jacksdiningroom, in a yellow 'YES CHEF' cap) drove two hours to try what he calls the best tacos in LA at Tacos Los Cholos, crediting T-Mobile Magenta Status for the easy rental car. At night by charcoal grills with intense flames, cooks grill thick ribeye steaks; he shows meat sliced on a wooden block, then tastes tacos topped with chopped onion and cilantro, calling the meat tender and exceptionally well-seasoned. He also opens a burrito with meat, cheese, and a sweet green pepper, pours house-made chipotle mayo inside, and praises the tortilla browning and overall flavor. Note: commenters point out the restaurant is in Anaheim/Orange County, not LA, and correct the pronunciation to 'Cholos.'

reels.title: The Interactive Map of Reddit
reels.summary: Becket U, a STEM resource aggregator, demos Andrei Kashcha's interactive Map of Reddit — a data visualization built from over 176 million Reddit comments. Each dot is a subreddit, with dot size reflecting community size, and similar subreddits cluster into themed 'countries' like Memelandia, Animeland, Furry Nation, and Pornlandia. Users can zoom in and click any dot to browse that community's top posts. The map is hosted on GitHub, and the caption notes this is the original version, with a 2023 update available. Kashcha presents it himself via screen recording with an upbeat explanatory voiceover.

reels.title: A Garlic Recipe No One Will Believe You Made
reels.summary: That Recipe (@thatrecipe.usa) makes an over-the-top garlicky fried dough snack with a deadpan instructional tone that plays like a parody of rage-bait cooking videos. They pour three egg yolks over a plate of peeled garlic cloves (150 g), blend it with a Milco immersion blender, then add 450 g wheat flour, salt, baking soda, parsley, 150 ml unsweetened natural yogurt, and two more whole eggs. The dough is kneaded, rolled out, cut into eight triangular wedges, and fried in a non-stick pan with vegetable oil until golden brown and crispy, served with dipping sauces. Comments fixate on the absurd garlic quantity and mock the pointless plate-transfer step. Caption: 'No one will believe the recipe you made with so much garlic.'

reels.title: Dostoevsky Author Guide: Where to Start
reels.summary: Rajlaxmi (ria) of @sentencesiloved presents a highly requested beginner's guide to Fyodor Dostoevsky as a series of slides with book covers and read-aloud plot/theme descriptions: 'White Nights,' 'Notes From Underground,' 'Crime and Punishment,' 'The Idiot,' 'Demons,' and 'The Brothers Karamazov.' A final 'REMEMBER' slide gives four study tips — patience, attention to symbolism, and reflective reading. The caption says her own introduction was 'Notes From Underground,' but she personally recommends starting with 'White Nights' because it's easier to get into his style, and notes she featured the Everyman's Library edition. Comments debate the best reading order and English translations.

reels.title: 3 Levels of Hot Chocolate
reels.summary: Kevin from KWOOWK (@letskwoowk) makes three levels of hot chocolate in a cozy kitchen tutorial. Level 1 is basic and nostalgic: heated milk with sugar and sifted cocoa powder, whisked and poured into a light-colored mug. Level 2 is French-style: chopped dark chocolate melted with cream, sugar, and salt, thinned with milk to a thick, smooth consistency, topped with whipped cream and grated chocolate. Level 3 is spiced: chopped dark chocolate, brown sugar, cinnamon sticks, and cardamom pods simmered in oat milk on low heat for about ten minutes to infuse, then whisked and adjusted with more milk, poured thick into a dark orange cup.
