reels.title: Delhi places list — monuments, metro & offbeat curiosities
reels.summary: Delhi-based creator Aryaman Sansanwal shares his list of Delhi places in a split-screen reel ('Pov- you're Delhi coded'): he speaks to camera in the top half while the bottom cycles through a campfire scene, a 'Gulab' fruit stand, a silver Delhi Metro train with a yellow stripe, streets with multilingual shop signs, a domed stone monument, a colorful fabric market, a tree-lined residential street, and a night-time street. The list mixes mood picks with curiosities — notably GB Road, which he says he doesn't want to enter but wants to see the area, its goings-on, and its crowd. Commenters confirm GB Road made the list and recommend a momos stall.

reels.title: Indian winter salad with coriander-chilli dressing
reels.summary: Chef Karan Arora's Indian winter salad: sliced cucumbers and radishes under a coriander-chili dressing made by grinding cumin seeds, roasted cumin powder, and green chilies in a marble mortar and pestle, then adding fresh coriander, garlic, rock salt, lemon juice, and extra-virgin olive oil. Health tip from the caption: soak the radish in water for 15–20 minutes if it's too pungent. Gluten-free, fiber-rich, and plant-based.

reels.title: Fried egg curry recipe
reels.summary: A fried egg curry tutorial from @maujes.food: fry an egg sprinkled with red chili powder in oil until golden brown, then set aside. Build the curry in a wok — oil, cumin and khade masale (whole spices), chopped onion, green chili, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala, tomato puree, and salt — add the fried eggs, cover, and cook. Finish with kasuri methi and fresh coriander.

reels.title: Hyderabadi dum chicken (Shadi wala red chicken)
reels.summary: Prachi Agarkar (@lets_eat_with_prachi) makes Hyderabadi dum chicken — 'Shadi wala red chicken' — as episode 3 of her non-vegetarian curries of India series. She marinates raw chicken pieces with yogurt, spices, and other ingredients, then sautés them in a saucepan with oil and water. She pitches it as an easy, beginner-friendly recipe that tastes spicy, tangy, and restaurant-style — 'straight from a restaurant' with minimal effort.

reels.title: Dal, bhaat & chokha — Bihar-style comfort meal
reels.summary: Bharat Wadhwa's 15-minute one-pot Bihar/UP comfort meal: yellow toor dal, rice and boiled potatoes pressure-cooked together for 4-5 whistles, finished with a tadka of red chilies, ginger-garlic paste and asafoetida, plus chokha made from a roasted tomato mashed with the potatoes, onion and the hot tempering, plated beside rice with dal ladled over. Pitched as a safe, time-saving single-pot method for bachelors and hostel dwellers — the caption jokes his cooker is 'completely safe', a claim commenters ironically riff on.

reels.title: 7 coffee hacks you probably didn't know
reels.summary: Ethan Rode's seven home-coffee hacks: a pinch of salt to cut bitterness; freezing brewed coffee in a silicone tray for dilution-free iced drinks; pumping a $10 French press as a milk frother for micro-foam; running hot water through a Nespresso before brewing to preheat it; making simple syrup from equal parts sugar and water (flavored with vanilla bean extract); and whisking the vanilla syrup with heavy cream and milk into a cold foam to layer on top. Gear shown includes a Breville espresso machine, AeroGadgets handheld frother, Pyrex measuring cup and Simply Organic vanilla extract.

reels.title: Railway-style tomato soup at home
reels.summary: Host Sahil (Your Food Lab) recreates the nostalgic Indian Railways tomato soup: saute cumin seeds, bay leaf, black cardamom, garlic, ginger, green chilies, onions, beetroot (for color) and tomatoes; add Kashmiri red chilli, coriander powder, cumin powder and black pepper; simmer, cool, puree and strain; then enrich with ketchup, lemon juice, chaat masala, sugar, butter and water before a final boil. Framed as a taste of long-distance train journeys, with commenters debating whether it can truly replicate the original Rajdhani/Shatabdi-era soup.

reels.title: The Office filming location in Panorama City
reels.summary: Aerial Google-Earth-style tour zeroing in on 13927 Saticoy Street in Panorama City, CA — the industrial building whose facade served as the Dunder Mifflin exterior in The Office (interiors were filmed on a soundstage), presented as a fan pilgrimage spot in a commercial-industrial zone near the 'Valley Center' sign. Commenters add insider detail — the property now operates as Quixote Chandler Valley under Sunset Studios — plus practical warnings that the surrounding neighborhood feels sketchy.

reels.title: Chicken chilli gravy
reels.summary: Restaurant chef Md Aajam Ansari demos chili chicken gravy in Hindi: heat oil in a wok, add ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, celery, onions and capsicum; then chili paste, tomato ketchup, dark soy sauce, green chili sauce, stock water, salt, sugar, white and black pepper, vinegar and corn flour to thicken; fold in cooked chicken and pack into a container. The comments turned it into a food-safety meme, roasting the cheap cooking oil as 'engine oil' and flagging the hot-food-in-plastic container as a health risk.

reels.title: Vegetarian mushroom galouti kebabs (Lucknow-style)
reels.summary: Chef Jeet Bisht's vegan take on Lucknow's Galouti kebab (born in Nawab Wajid Ali Shah's royal kitchens, famed for melt-in-the-mouth texture): fry 3 onions and 1/2 cup cashews golden; blend 400g boiled mushrooms into a paste and saute until the moisture evaporates; mix in the onion-cashew paste with 1/2 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp cardamom, 1 tsp garam masala, salt and 2-3 tbsp roasted chana dal powder for binding; shape into patties and pan-fry in ghee until golden. Served with ulte tawa parathas — while the comments are full of sarcastic jabs at the very idea of a vegetarian galouti.

reels.title: Southwest road trip: LA through Zion and beyond
reels.summary: Alex Khachigian's numbered Southwest road trip starting from LA: Death Valley, Las Vegas, Valley of Fire, Zion, Bryce Canyon, Belly of the Dragon, Sand Caves, Old Paria, Toadstool Hoodoos, White Pocket, Buckskin Gulch and Horseshoe Bend — with optional extensions to Antelope Canyon (permit required), Lake Powell, Grand Canyon, Flagstaff and Sedona. The caption lists stops in driving order, and commenters add practical detail on realistic trip length, entrance fees and pet policies.

reels.title: Dada ji casual meme
reels.summary: Bait-and-switch Hindi meme: a weary monologue of an old man craving 3-4 cigarettes and lamenting his health plays over unrelated glossy clips (a suited silhouette adjusting sunglasses, a stage performer with a mic), captioned 'Dada ji tarika thoda casual tha'. The somber-audio-versus-absurd-visuals mismatch is the joke — while prominent WINMATCH.COM overlays and tags reveal it's also a stealth promo for an online gambling platform.

reels.title: Driving Highway 395 through the Eastern Sierra
reels.summary: Grant's scenic Highway 395 reel through the Eastern Sierra, with snow-covered Mount Whitney (14,000+ ft) towering over the high desert. The caption is a full route guide: take Highway 14 north from SoCal through Palmdale and Lancaster to Mojave (the last affordable fuel stop), pass Red Rock Canyon State Park ('the Bryce Canyon of California'), then join 395 north through Lone Pine (Whitney Portal Road), Big Pine (junction to the White Mountains and Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest), Bishop and Mammoth Lakes. Commenters debate whether 395 beats Highway 1 and add fuel, speed-trap and road-condition tips.

reels.title: Mattha ke aloo — UP-special potato curry
reels.summary: shweta suzzy's (Foodiesuppy) UP-style Mattha ke Aloo: whisk Amul Masti dahi with water into a batter; temper cumin, asafoetida and green chilies in mustard oil with turmeric, coriander powder and Kashmiri red chili; fold in boiled potatoes, add the dahi batter and simmer to a boil; finish with fresh coriander and kasuri methi, served in a metal cup with papadums. Billed as a 'World Famous Recipe' — while the comments roast the excessive water and joke about the curd splitting.
reels.creator_name: shweta suzzy🔥 ( Prayagraj) U Tube 65k,Moj 4Lakh, Facebook 100k

reels.title: Underrated homeware companies
reels.summary: Nolan White's roundup of three underrated homeware brands: Puebco (Japan) — upcycled goods from reclaimed parachutes, military canvas and recycled aluminum, including a striped tote, ceramic bath set and parachute tissue cover; Utilitario (Mexico) — playful bright kitchen goods like enamel dishware, aluminum cups, a colorful egg basket and a cast-aluminum tortilla press; and Italic — direct-to-consumer products from the same factories as luxury brands, cutting marketing spend, e.g. wine glasses, a cashmere throw and bath towels he personally owns. Commenters want price transparency (the $85 tortilla press drew fire) and more specifics.

reels.title: Extreme horror movies that test your limits
reels.summary: Horror creator Elaine Frost's 'Four More Horror Movies That Altered My Brain': Passion (2018), billed as a heavey-shing walk through the uncanny valley that 'looks like a m*stered st*nd', and Takashi Miike's Ichi the Killer (2001) — 'a contender for the most depraved film of all time' — featured in two segments. Her caption urges viewers to look up trigger warnings and go in blind. The comments are full of Miike worship ('All hail Miike') and debate over Ichi the Killer's genre classification.

reels.title: Copycat McDonald's Chicken McGrill burger
reels.summary: MasterChef India winner Prachi Agarkar recreates the discontinued mid-2000s Indian McDonald's Chicken McGrill — the Rs 20 'spicy chatpata Indianised burger' with grilled chicken patty, mint mayo, onion and tomato that she and her cousin saved pocket money for. Her copycat: chicken mince mixed with ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chilli, coriander, mint leaves, cumin, black pepper, salt, egg white and breadcrumbs, shaped and shallow-fried; pudina chutney blended with mayonnaise as the mint mayo; assembled on a sesame-seed bun with onion and tomato slices. Commenters confirm the original still survives in Delhi and the North (now ~Rs 100) but not in Mumbai, Gujarat or South India — and many are petitioning McDonald's India to bring it back nationwide.

reels.title: Growing leafy greens in containers — Grow It Yourself ep. 4
reels.summary: ABHINAV YADAV's Grow It Yourself episode 4: leafy greens as the easiest first pick for container gardening, harvest-ready in 45-60 days. The soil mix is garden soil (40%), vermicompost (30%), cocopeat (20%) and construction sand (10%), optionally enriched with neem khali, cow dung ash or bonemeal; sow in broad shallow pots (12 inch x 6 inch) — crush coriander seeds and soak all seeds (except coriander) overnight. His tips: dust haldi or cinnamon powder into the mix as an antifungal, cover seeds with only a thin soil layer, water with a sprayer, keep in indirect light until germination then move to morning sun, and keep soil moist, not wet. Recommended first seeds: spinach, methi, pak choi, dhaniya and soya.

reels.title: Joshua Tree hippie greenscreen commentary
reels.summary: Blond in Car's deadpan greenscreen 'A Mom's Guide to Joshua Tree' — an ironic beginner's guide to an iconic destination, framed as a reply to a viewer who joked about having to Google what a Joshua tree is. She covers the game of spotting the first Joshua tree for ice cream, the Cholla Cactus Garden (commenters correct her 'chola' pronunciation), and Pappy & Harriet's music venue with its hipster-biker-desert-rat crowd and Neutral Milk Hotel history. Commenters add the practical warning that drug use is restricted on federal land.

reels.title: 24-hour dal makhani
reels.summary: Sanjana Modha's 24-hour dal makhani: soak black urad lentils, add saffron, garam masala, butter, onion, mint and soy sauce, then pressure-cook in an Instant Pot for up to 15 hours and finish with crème fraîche and a vigorous beat for a buttery 'liquid velvet' texture. A 24-hour process with minimal active effort — full recipe and measurements on sanjanafeasts.co.uk. Commenters debate the ideal cook time (6 vs 15 hours), ask about stovetop and dairy-free adaptations, and confirm the cooker is a UK-model Instant Pot.

reels.title: 5 software engineering whitepapers worth reading
reels.summary: InterviewReady founder Gaurav Sen's five software-engineering whitepapers worth reading, ranked: 5. Facebook TAO, 4. Google Filesystem, 3. Google BigTable, 2. Facebook Memcached, 1. Google Zanzibar. It's also a promo for his live whitepaper-reading classes at @interviewready_, with the next session on Google Zanzibar scheduled for February 4, 2024. Commenters confirm the papers are publicly available, suggest additions like DynamoDB and Amazon database papers, and note that Zanzibar is Turing-complete.

reels.title: Space-saving kitchen & pantry organization (Amazon)
reels.summary: Julianna Christensen's space-saving kitchen organization showcase, all from her Amazon storefront's 'Kitchen Organization' section: a rotating 360° multi-compartment dry-food dispenser that portion-dispenses six foods (quinoa, rice, popcorn kernels) at the press of a button; peel-and-stick pull-out cabinet drawers with a two-minute install in multiple sizes; and a slim four-tier rolling pantry cart for tight spaces, styled with fruit. Also announces giveaway winners @natalie.eileen1 and @alyssaraerios — while the comments are a flood of purchase-link requests.

reels.title: Caramelised onion dip with flatbread chips
reels.summary: Plant-based cook Alfie Steiner's caramelised onion dip, framed as January comfort food: dice 2-3 white onions and cook low and slow for 30-45 minutes in Flora plant-based butter and olive oil (deglazing with water), then mix with 200g Violife cream cheese, 2 tbsp Hellmann's plant-based mayo, garlic, chives, pickles, parsley, lemon juice, salt, pepper and smoked paprika, finished with olive oil and chives. Served with homemade flatbread chips; full recipe in the caption. Playful touches include the 'if you stick your tongue out, you stop crying' onion-chopping hack and a cameo from a co-star reacting to the dip.

reels.title: The best fruits for fiber and antioxidants
reels.summary: Internal medicine doctor Lauren DeDecker MD rates fruits in a Whole Foods aisle: all whole fruit is good, but high-fiber, high-antioxidant picks win for satiety, gut health and anti-aging — berries top the list for antioxidants. Grapes are high-sugar and middling; cherries are praised for antioxidants and pre-workout use; oranges bring fiber and antioxidants; apples offer gut-friendly pectin; pears are high-fiber; melons (cantaloupe, pineapple, honeydew, watermelon) are low-fiber but hydrating and still fine; and two kiwis a day can relieve constipation. She stresses choosing whole over dried fruit — and admits her personal favorite is jackfruit, worth the trek to an Asian market.

reels.title: Steak & Bones Tacos in Hillcrest, San Diego
reels.summary: Foodie nurse Melski reviews Steak & Bones Tacos in Hillcrest, San Diego (open about a year): the $10 ribeye 'Steak and Bones' taco (grilled ribeye on the bone, caramelized cheese crust, guacamole) and the $9 'Bad to the Bone' taco (bone-in beef braised three hours in adobo, falling off the bone, with pickled onions), plus carne asada Steak & Bones nachos. She praises the reasonable prices, made-to-order tortillas and the salsa bar — singling out the mango salsa. The full menu runs chicken, adobada ($5), T.J. ($5), don sirloin and more, narrated by Chef Caesar Sanchez.

reels.title: Potato guide: which type for which dish
reels.summary: Mike Cowley's starch-based potato guide: high-starch russets are for baking and frying (fluffy interior, crispy exterior) but make waterlogged, grainy mash; medium-starch Yukon Golds give creamy mashed potatoes and roast well; low-starch red potatoes hold their shape in stews and potato salads but shouldn't be mashed (a claim commenters contest). He clarifies sweet potatoes aren't true potatoes — slipping in the 'sometimes shaped like a dog' meme — and wields a DeWalt drill as a prop while pitching @dewalttough for a sponsorship. Commenters add varieties (Kennebec, King Edward, purple), note diabetics prefer red potatoes, and suggest steaming russets before mashing.

reels.title: Invitation-only Indonesian restaurant — 2024 bookings update
reels.summary: WarungRieRie announces its 2024 booking system is full through December: the invitation-only Indonesian restaurant in San Diego's Serra Mesa serves a six-course organic garden meal inside a rice hut shipped from Bali — billed as San Diego's hardest reservation. The earliest opening was Friday, Jan 12 at 4 PM (book by calling 619-208-0384); beyond that it's weekly Monday-evening cancellation posts and a waitlist via the website's contact form. A reposted review from @suzionthemove describes driving 3 miles and feeling like she'd flown 16 hours to Bali, snagging her table from a cancellation.

reels.title: IKEA kitchen organization ideas for 2024
reels.summary: IKEA-based kitchen organization ideas pitched as a 2024 fresh-start resolution for apartment living — specific products are shown on screen but no details are given in the caption beyond the ikeahack framing.

reels.title: Product 89 — kitchen gadget (comment 'Link' to shop)
reels.summary: CTA-only Amazon affiliate reel for 'Product 89' — a kitchen dispenser/gadget shown in the video; comment 'Link' to shop, with all product links in the bio's 'Amazon 1-100' storefront and highlights. No product details are given in the caption beyond the kitchen-hashtag framing.

reels.title: Homemade San Marzano pizza sauce
reels.summary: Tom Judkins' (thebkydpalate) San Marzano pizza sauce, which he swears beats store-bought: one 28oz can of Cento San Marzano tomatoes (broken chunky by hand or immersion blender) with sauteed 1/2 yellow onion, 1-3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp basil, 1/2 tsp oregano, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar and a pinch of crushed red pepper; optionally simmered 20 minutes for a deeper, less acidic flavor and good in the fridge for two weeks. The video demos it on a backyard patio — dough stretched by hand, sauce spread, mozzarella and Hormel Pepperoni Cup Crisp Bold, baked on a pizza stone in an Ooni oven. Commenters ignite a sarcastic pizza-orthodoxy war over the sugar.

reels.title: Old Geiger Grade road history — Reno to Virginia City
reels.summary: All-Terrain Dude's guide to the historic Geiger Toll Road from Reno to Virginia City, Nevada: built in 1862 with way stations to haul Comstock ore to the mills (the newer Geiger Grade alignment came in 1936, but he prefers the original). The volunteer-maintained dirt route is passable year-round in the dry climate but gets rough and rutted; his directions start on I-580 south from Reno, exiting at Virginia City/Mount Rose onto Toll Road past the 'Foot of the Grade' barn. Drone footage shows his silver Toyota Tacoma on the winding grade — and commenters confirm even a stock Honda Ridgeline has made it, while others worry the exposure will spoil the trail's solitude.

reels.title: 2023 Amazon best sellers — top 10 home items
reels.summary: Danielle Santana's 'Amazon FTW: 2023 Best Sellers' — her top 10 home items, from a 99% natural USA-made cleaning paste and a multifunctional pen (level, ruler, light, stylus, screwdriver, bottle opener) to absorbent clay mats, wireless motion-sensor under-cabinet lights, washing-machine cleaning pods, magnetic bookmarks, a single-screw soft-close cabinet hinge, waterproof playing cards, a fade-and-stain-resistant cooling pillow and septic-friendly garbage-disposal cleaner. Hosted from her car; the comments are dominated by link requests.

reels.title: AF Chicken — creamy bell pepper fusion
reels.summary: Home chef Afshan's 'AF Chicken' — a creamy bell-pepper fusion chicken: season chicken with salt, lemon juice and vinegar and marinate 15-20 minutes; heat butter with cumin seeds and ginger-garlic paste; cook the chicken to 80%; add onions, bell peppers and green chilies; season with coriander and cumin powders plus salt; then pour in cream, garam masala and kasuri methi and simmer briefly. Commenters rave about his soothing voice (likened to Adnan Sami), ask about yogurt-for-cream swaps, and fixate on the BB King 'Thrill Is Gone' playing in the background.

reels.title: Favorite pizza spots in San Diego
reels.summary: San Diego foodie Danielle's (throughmybrownglasses) favorite pizza joints, part 1 of a series: Caliano Pizza (Chula Vista), Square Pizza Co. (Pacific Beach), Hillcrust Pizza (Hillcrest), Prince Street Pizza (Downtown Gaslamp), Pizza Cassette (Morena) and Best Pizza & Brew (Mira Mesa) — no ranking implied, just her personal picks. Set to Justin Bieber's 'Baby'; part 2 promised. Commenters treat it as a debate starter, most notably demanding to know why Bronx Pizza was omitted and pitching their own additions like Zia's and Tribute Pizza.

reels.title: Favorite fashion brands right now
reels.summary: Nolan White's 'dream closet' — his favorite menswear brands if money were no object: Stoffa (effortless elegance, flowy airy fabrics), Huson's Paris (sexy 1970s tailoring in a Gucci/Tom Ford/YSL vein), Evan Kinnory (heavier, blockier, earthy Californian craftsmanship), Orly (experimental lighting, flowy silhouettes, bold trims), Taiga Takahashi (the CSM graduate pulling vintage 1800s details into contemporary designs) and Komoli (Japanese, 'heavy when you want it to be, light when you don't'). Commenters want price points and on-screen labels, suggest affordable alternatives, and a few call out high-end gatekeeping.

reels.title: Y2K room decor ideas
reels.summary: Krop Store's 'Cool sh*t you need in your room Pt.283' — a rapid catalog of statement decor with price overlays: a $120 white Lego Porsche, a Tom and Jerry rug, a cloud sofa, an 'Explosion Lamp' shaped like a nuclear blast, a 'Yeezus Table' in Kanye West album-art graphics, a Formula 1 car suspended from a dining-room ceiling for $3.5 million, and a $30 Spotify rug. The comments treat the extravagant prices as comedy, roasting the fantasy that 'money grows on trees'.

reels.title: Tandoori pomfret for ₹250 in Noida
reels.summary: Tandoori pomfret for Rs 250 at Indie BBQ (shop A03, Futech Gateway Society Market, Sector 75, Noida), grilled by a chef in a 'DINNER IS COMING' apron. The comments complicate the deal: the Rs 250 price was a December-January promotion (now Rs 350), some report stale fish and 90-minute waits, and a heated halal-vs-jhatka debate over the seafood drew an owner clarification that it's neither. The outlet sits adjacent to Haven International Coffee House.

reels.title: Best seekh kebabs in Delhi
reels.summary: Sameer Bawa declares kebab season officially on and hunts Delhi's best seekh kebabs, calling them 'absolutely brilliant' — the specific spots are named in the video, not the caption.

reels.title: Amazon home finds — comment 'Links' to shop
reels.summary: Timothy & Tatyana Ramjohn's Amazon Home find: a white sink cabinet with wooden countertop hiding two concealed pull-out trash cans (with liners), plus drawer storage and countertop space styled as a tea/coffee station. Comment 'Links' for an auto-DM with the purchase link. Commenters can't resist the joke — a coffee station sitting atop hidden trash cans.

reels.title: 10x your health — daily detox swaps
reels.summary: Danica's 'TIPS TO 10X YOUR HEALTH' is a split-screen meme: a woman calmly eats fruit salad while a man's deadpan voice-over lists toxin-avoidance swaps — stainless steel and glass, ditch air fresheners, a tight-weave cotton shower curtain, carbon-filtered water — punctuated by absurdities like 'take a scuba tank' (followed by 'kidding on that one'). The caption is earnest by contrast: avoid tap water and plastics, beware 'forever chemicals', and detox with the natural mineral zeolite clinoptilolite, whose structure and charge supposedly trap them.

reels.title: Mushroom masala recipe
reels.summary: Sagar Kumar's (Sagar's Kitchen) Mushroom Masala — 'make it once and forget the rest': marinate 400g halved button mushrooms with fried onion paste, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic-green-chili paste, coriander powder, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, mutton masala, 150g curd, coriander leaves and salt for 5 minutes; heat 2 tbsp mustard oil with cumin seeds, whole spices (stone flower, star anise, cloves, cardamom, black cardamom, mace, 2 bay leaves) and 1 tbsp Kashmiri red chili powder; saute the mushrooms 3-4 minutes, then cover and cook on low for 15-17 minutes. No tomato, no water. Commenters rave about the restaurant-style result — and about the creator's sing-song South-Indian-influenced Hindi delivery ('sachchi bata raha hai', 'ayo') as much as the recipe.

reels.title: Charred whole cabbage with roasted garlic
reels.summary: Chef Saransh Goila's smoky charred cabbage, inspired by a Hispic (sweet-heart) cabbage he ate at Mackie Mayor in Manchester two years earlier: quarter the cabbage, roast in 1 tbsp mustard oil covered for 6-8 minutes until caramelized and charred; make a dressing from a crushed pod of roasted garlic, mint, coriander, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, coriander powder, garam masala, salt, black pepper, 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar, lemon juice and 3 tbsp olive oil; pour half over the wedges and cook 3-4 more minutes; whisk the rest into 1 cup thick yogurt, spread on a plate, top with the cabbage and garnish with pickled onions, boondi and coriander — 'Delishaaas'. Comments split between enthusiasm and tapeworm/food-safety worries, with the chef advising a salted-water soak to wash the cabbage.

reels.title: Tadka focaccia — no-knead, Indian-spiced
reels.summary: Rishi Nanavati — dentist, former private chef and MasterChef quarterfinalist — fuses Italian focaccia with an Indian tadka: mix bread flour, water, yeast and salt into a sticky no-knead dough; do four rounds of stretch-and-fold with 15-minute rests; cold-proof for better texture and flavor. Saute mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, garlic and green chilies in oil, then dimple-press the hot tadka into the dough on an oiled tray and bake as hot as possible until golden. Best eaten fresh (or reheated); his favorite serve is tadka focaccia chutney sandwiches. Full recipe on his blog. Commenters call it 'genius' and ask about all-purpose-flour swaps.

reels.title: Reviewing Community Goods (coffee)
reels.summary: LA food reviewer Kevin Noparvar's deadpan car review of Community Goods, 'the most hyped up shop in LA right now': he opens by saying he wanted to call it 'overhyped and the worst thing ever', then praises the signature breakfast sliders as 'cloud-like' and 'melting in your mouth', declares the banana bread with passion-fruit butter 'the star of the show', and lands on an 8.2/10. The monotone delivery against enthusiastic adjectives — plus exaggerated post-bite moans — is the joke.

reels.title: Portable foldable electric drying rack (Amazon)
reels.summary: Julianna Christensen's Amazon find: a portable, foldable, electric 3-tier drying rack — 43% off plus a 5% coupon — for jeans, sweaters, delicates, bedding and winter gear, with built-in timers, folding flat into a closet. Listed in her AMZ storefront's 'Laundry Favorites' section; the $100 Amazon gift card giveaway is closed (winner @vinodhinic).

reels.title: Presence, flow state and mindfulness
reels.summary: A bearded creator from The Mental Level guides a grounding meditation from a night-time subway platform: notice the tingling in your feet, the sensation in your hands, the ambient sounds; visualize the room without moving your eyes; breathe deeply and relax your muscles — shifting from distraction to flow state. The caption jokes 'You might start tap dancing', and the video points viewers to The Mental Level's YouTube for longer practices. Commenters riff on the visceral foot-tingling descriptions.

reels.title: Amazon cleaning finds that make cleaning fun
reels.summary: Samantha Numan's (sam.shan.shops) Amazon cleaning showcase centers on the Dyson V15 Detect Absolute cordless vacuum: laser light that reveals invisible dust, wet-and-dry pickup, an anti-tangle roller head, a digital battery display and over an hour and twenty minutes of runtime, demoed on hardwood, tile and carpet with the dustbin emptied on camera. 'Cleaning just became kinda fun'. Commenters mock the $900-1,000 price tag and compare it to the Dyson V11 Animal, Tineco and Shark.

reels.title: San Diego's secret topiary garden
reels.summary: Daniella Bragg's hidden-gem pick: Harper's Topiary Garden in Mission Hills, San Diego — designed by the couple who live in the house above, inspired by topiary gardens they saw on their travels. The garden changes with the seasons (even cooler at Halloween with lights), and there's a free little library plus a downtown view. Pitched as a spot most locals don't know, perfect for photos.

reels.title: Amazon laundry room finds — What I Bought Wednesday
reels.summary: Allie Hunter's 'What I Bought Wednesday – Laundry Room Edition': a gray TROMM magnetic laundry card with silicone gap cover for behind the washer/dryer, a KOAN lint bin, ACTIVE washing-machine cleaner tablets, a pink mesh bra bag that protects up to five bras, a magnetic front-load dryer door pog with flexible stem for airflow and odor prevention, and a black retractable hanger with 18 hooks and a sliding bar for small laundry areas. Comment 'Laundry1' for DM links; everything also linked in stories.

reels.title: Top 23 Amazon finds of 2023
reels.summary: Arielle Brimhall's 'Amazon Top 23 Products of 2023' (Pt. 1): products shown include the Scrub Daddy Damp Duster, an adhesive outlet switch, a rechargeable motion-sensor light, adhesive wall baskets, a travel extension cord, a DeWEISN portable vanity mirror and a reusable lint roller. Comment '2023' for a DM with the shoppable link (or shop her storefront's 'Top 23 of 2023' list). She answers a commenter that a hair dryer's heat safely removes the baskets' adhesive from wall paint.

reels.title: Cinder Cone hike in Lassen — Painted Dunes views
reels.summary: Alex Khachigian's 'the one hike you need to do in California': Cinder Cone, a 200-foot volcanic cone in Lassen Volcanic National Park formed in two eruptions in the 1650s, with summit views of the Fantastic Lava Beds and the colorful Painted Dunes. The trail is 3 hours round trip (4 miles) with a steep incline, reached via a 6-mile off-road drive to Butte Lake Campground; drive times run 10 hours from LA and 4 from San Francisco. Commenters warn about the loose volcanic gravel ('two steps forward, one step back') and seasonal closures.

reels.title: 5 epic California drives for your bucket list
reels.summary: Alex Khachigian's five bucket-list California drives: Morro Bay (Morro Rock), Mattole Road along the Lost Coast (Sugarloaf Island), Carson Pass Highway (Silver Lake), Squaw Valley (Olympic Valley) and Shoreline Highway near Elk — 'the last one is EPIC'. Commenters note Morro Bay has grown congested, praise the Elk drive as a hidden gem, and nominate additions like Union Ave in Bakersfield.

reels.title: Joshua Tree Christmas tips — skip the lines
reels.summary: Visit Joshua Tree's Christmas-visit tips, delivered via a serious-cat meme of a traffic jam ('ME: I told you to not to use the Joshua Tree entrance to the park!'): (1) at mid-day on holidays, use the 29 Palms entrance — 12 miles east on Highway 62, hardly ever a line, and closer to many park destinations; (2) park gates are open 24 hours, so you can enter even unattended (have your receipt or pass ready at exit); (3) the three entrances are Joshua Tree (west), 29 Palms (north) and Cottonwood/Hwy 10 (south); (4) buy a pass online or at a visitor center — a day pass is good for seven days, plus annual and senior lifetime options. Also: pack out trash, no dogs on trails, no off-roading, limited cell service, no water or stores in the park — bring lots of water. Commenters confirm the 29 Palms shortcut and share a 4x4 alternative via Berdoo Canyon.

reels.title: Spending real time in the Redwoods
reels.summary: Adventure couple Lucas & Kelsey Smissen on why driving straight through the Redwoods was a mistake: a map zooms from Earth to the Avenue of the Giants, playing out a scripted exchange — his wife wants to see 'the tallest trees in the world', he replies 'Say no more!' — then cuts to an aerial of the winding road through towering redwoods with a lone figure in a yellow jacket, all scored ironically to Bruce Springsteen's 'Dancing in the Dark'. The caption admits their first trip rushed through the trees; this time they stayed for 'absolutely epic memories'. Commenters add that the Avenue is part of Highway 101 and redwoods are the world's tallest trees.

reels.title: Stunning non-national-park spots on the West Coast
reels.summary: Porsche 911 road-tripper Jeff Rhoades' four favorite non-national-park West Coast spots: Leslie Gulch in Oregon's Jordan Valley (end of 25 miles of rough gravel in the SE Oregon Outback — spectacular, no crowds); the High Steel Bridge in Washington (the tallest railroad bridge ever built in the US, 375 feet above the South Fork of the Skokomish River in the Olympic National Forest, converted to car traffic in the 1960s and accessible to any car); Alabama Hills near Lone Pine, CA (movie filming location off US 395 with rock formations, dispersed camping and '911 friendly' trails under the Eastern Sierra); and Burney Falls, which Teddy Roosevelt called 'the 8th Wonder of the World' (McArthur-Burney Falls State Park on CA 89, near Lassen). Set to Vaughan Williams' 'The Lark Ascending'; shot on a DJI Mini 3 Pro.

reels.title: Chana masala chakhna recipe
reels.summary: Roshan mishra's (mast_mola_kitchen) veg chakna — a North Indian chickpea snack curry: heat oil on an iBELL induction cooktop, sizzle cinnamon and cardamom, saute sliced onions, add ginger-garlic paste and pre-soaked chickpeas, season with cumin, coriander, turmeric, red chili, black salt and garam masala, add water and simmer covered; garnish with coriander, lemon and whole green chilies. The caption says make it for your papa and his eyes will fill with tears — a veg version he made for his dad after his earlier chakna videos hit 25M and 15M views. The Hindi narration ends with a playful 'khamba kholna' innuendo punchline.

reels.title: Anza-Borrego Desert at sunset — Fonts Point
reels.summary: Grace's (grraceface) winter sunset at Fonts Point in Anza-Borrego Desert State Park — 'a quick drive to Mars': the sun dips behind eroded badlands, turning the sky an 'apocalyptic blaze' of pink, orange and purple in first-person and aerial shots. An all-wheel-drive ride is the way in for the sandy off-road trails. Tagged #LeaveNoTrace; commenters joke about Teslas in soft sand and the 'scary movie' pose of the lone ridge figure.

reels.title: Feather River Canyon scenic byway
reels.summary: Alex Khachigian's 'most underrated drive in California': the Feather River Canyon Scenic Byway (SR 70) climbing into the Sierra Nevada, with sheer-walled canyons up to 1,000 feet above the river, granite boulders and waterfall cascades. Must-sees: Pulga Bridges, Grizzly Dome Tunnel, Rock Creek Trestle, Tobin Bridge and historic train tracks; drive times range from 2 hours (Sacramento) to 9.5 (San Diego). Commenters warn to check conditions — Dixie Fire damage, construction, rock slides and seasonal closures.

reels.title: Favorite car-DIY YouTube channels (Part 3)
reels.summary: Stefanie Dechant's part 3 of favorite car-DIY YouTube channels — 'like having a personal mechanic in your pocket': Donut, ChrisFix, The Engineers Post, GRIP – Das Motormagazin, Auto BILD, Automann-TV and auto motor und sport, spanning flat fixes to complex engine work (some in German, with English subtitles available). Commenters endorse Donut and ChrisFix as the 'goats', share repair success stories, and expand the list with Throttle House, Hagerty, Engineering Explained, Scotty Kilmer and more.

reels.title: Organizing my spice cabinet (Amazon)
reels.summary: Decor Delights organizes her spice cabinet with Amazon products shown on screen — comment for the link; no further details in the caption.

reels.title: Cheap date ideas in Orange County — most saved of 2023
reels.summary: LOCALE magazine's 'Cheap Date Ideas in Orange County' — their most saved reel of 2023: Sherman Gardens in Corona del Mar ($5), OCMA in Costa Mesa (free), the OC Zoo in Orange ($2), Noguchi Gardens in Costa Mesa (free), the castle at Victoria Beach in Laguna Beach (free), Hidden House Coffee in San Juan Capistrano ($5) and the Balboa Ferry in Newport Beach ($2). Commenters flag hidden costs (OCMA parking) and debate the OC Zoo's animal welfare.

reels.title: Amazon home favorites roundup
reels.summary: Synclaire Lawson's (linenoaksinteriors) 2023 Amazon Home favorites roundup — 'game changers' for a cozy, elevated home: a coffee table, vintage bench, sideboard, bed pillows, rug pad, fruit bowl, swivel chairs, rug, mug, books, spice jars, fabric shaver, trash bin, bath caddy and duvet insert. Comment 'shop' for links.

reels.title: Racing History Cinematic Universe watch order
reels.summary: Movie analyst Anhar Karim's watch-order guide for the 'Racing History Cinematic Universe' — spanning Ferrari (with Adam Driver) and Michael Mann's racing films — the actual order is laid out in the video, not the caption.

reels.title: Route of the Hiawatha trail
reels.summary: Arnel Culum's look at the Route of the Hiawatha — 15 miles of scenic trails and historic tunnels; the ride is in the video.

reels.title: Creepy YouTube video essays & documentaries
reels.summary: monse's (cvnela) meme-format list of 'my top disturbing documentaries' on YouTube: the infamous Nasubi livestream (a Japanese contestant confined for months, surviving on contest prizes — shown as a shirtless man holding a PlayStation) and a bodycam video of a man discovering a killer in his attic (the 'Bodycam' meme). 'The second one made me cry', she captions, with hashtags hinting at a Japan-and-Mexico cross-cultural focus. The suspenseful electronic track and numbered listicle format package genuinely traumatic footage as binge-watch material.

reels.title: Bhogal's Chole Bhature, CP Delhi
reels.summary: Kashika Garg (swadishtdelights) tags chole bhature lovers from the iconic 85-year-old Bhogal's in Connaught Place, Delhi — 'jb bhi Delhi jaungi, I'll have them for sure' — crediting @platter_and_paths and @thefoodiequila for the find.

reels.title: Bread & toast experience in Tokyo
reels.summary: Chef Saransh Goila's 'bread and toast experience' at Center the Bakery in Ginza, Tokyo: pillowy shokupan (Japanese milk bread) with a private vintage toaster, five colorful jams and loads of butter, plus an egg sando, French toast, cinnamon sugar toast and a 'sensational' cheese toast. 'Have you ever tried a bread and toast experience in your life? If not, you must change that' — he declares it 'bread heaven'. Commenters announce Tokyo travel plans and ask for similar experiences in India.

reels.title: Saoji cuisine at Orange City, Mumbai
reels.summary: Socialruffian's showcase of Nagpur's Saoji cuisine at Orange City Saoji, Juhu Circle, Mumbai — with 15% off the bill for showing the reel. The Nagpur-native owner makes the masalas in-house; signatures include Saoji Green Mutton Curry, Tarri sauce, Kaleji Dry, Bheja Masala, Saoji Khur (Paya) Thali, garlic rice, Saoji Mutton Dry and Saoji Sundari Dry, averaging Rs 800 for two — with Remo D'Souza name-checked as a frequent guest. The comments split: excitement over the fiery novelty versus complaints of excessive oil, bland items, inattentive service and the discount not being honored.

reels.title: DIY $20 chess board wall hook
reels.summary: Lone Fox's Drew Michael Scott turns a ~$20 Vamslove 3-in-1 wooden game board into a wall-mounted coat rack in about 30 minutes: inspired by Peter Marigold's 'Coat Check' artwork (saved on Pinterest for years), he marks each piece's position with blue painter's tape, drills pilot holes, and screws the chess pieces into the board as hooks — the knights becoming 'little horse heads' — with picture hangers on the top corners. Fully customizable (arrange a favorite position or a famous end-game); pitched as a DIY Christmas gift for an entryway or bedroom. Chess fans in the comments are playfully outraged.
reels.creator_name: Lone Fox by Drew Michael Scott

reels.title: Indian Canyons hike near Palm Springs
reels.summary: Marteen (lustfortheworld) finally explores Indian Canyons near Palm Springs after five years of festival and San Jacinto trips — 'maybe I saved the best for last': a 2.7-mile, 365-foot-elevation hike (10 minutes from downtown Palm Springs, 2.5 hours from San Diego) through a dense palm forest to a clear stream, billed as 'a little slice of paradise', set to smooth jazz sax. Commenters add practical notes — the trail is on a fee-based Indian reservation, bring walking sticks for river crossings — and spark a debate over reservation land use.

reels.title: California's most beautiful drives — SoCal edition (Part 2)
reels.summary: Asya Olson's (asyatravels) Part 2 of California's most beautiful drives, SoCal edition: 1) San Diego to Julian with a Sunrise Highway detour at Mt. Laguna ('one of the prettiest drives in California'); 2) Park Boulevard through Joshua Tree (Hidden Valley, Skull Rock); 3) Hwy 178 from Bakersfield to Isabella Lake along the Kern River — a windy, cliffside hidden gem; 4) Carrizo Plain National Monument at its springtime yellow super-bloom (her clip is from March 25); 5) Hwy 101 from Gaviota to Ventura for ocean views. She plugs her California map (link in bio) and asks what should make Part 3.

reels.title: Royal Maharashtrian thali near Lonavala
reels.summary: Royal Maharashtrian village-style dining at Hotel Shauryawada in Lonavala (Waksai), 10 minutes from Lonavala's 2nd exit on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway: signature Mutton Raan at Rs 1,850, Chicken Raan at Rs 799, and non-veg thaals from Rs 330 with Gauran-style gravies. The regal, spacious multi-cuisine outlet has also expanded to Pune.

reels.title: Motoring Coffee — cool LA coffee spot
reels.summary: Motoring Coffee in LA — a hybrid coffee shop and car showroom with a Porsche 911, Toyota Land Cruiser FJ40, Rolls-Royce limo and a kei truck repurposed as a table, in an industrial space with green-tiled walls and a marble counter. The coffee counter is open to the public, but the car collection sits behind a membership (~$200 initiation plus $100/month). 'A cool lil spot to do some work or catch up with friends' — though commenters rate the coffee as average and prefer the matcha.

reels.title: California road trips — best time of year for each
reels.summary: Preethi Chandrasekhar's (eagertravele) seasonal guide to seven California bucket-list road trips: Kings Canyon June-September; Big Sur all year (road closures permitting); Death Valley November-March; Mt Shasta June-September for hiking; Yosemite May-October — plus February for the firefall; Alabama Hills June-September; Redwood National Park all year. Commenters trade winter-Yosemite experiences and flag fire closures and flooding.

reels.title: Vapor Slide vs Tabletop Drifters — RC drift comparison
reels.summary: A desk-side comparison of two RC drift cars: the larger Tabletop Drifter (1:76 scale, rear-wheel drive, tunable gyro, fully proportional throttle and steering, multiple tuning options — best for indoor desktop use) versus the smaller Vapor Slide (all-wheel drive, simpler controller with a dedicated vapor button, no gyro — easier for beginners, better on larger living-room floors). Commenters add pricing (~$125 for the minis, ~$65 for larger), ~30-minute battery life, out-of-stock frustrations, ~$75 AliExpress alternatives, and scam/non-delivery accusations.

reels.title: India's #1 sim racing pedals — Simforge
reels.summary: Endurance racer Jamie Shaw promotes Simforge Engineering's Mark-1 pedals — 'India's #1 sim racing pedals', made in Pune: Formula-1-grade 150kg brake pressure with quick-fix adjustable stiffness, at less than a quarter of global competitors' prices and with no import tax for Indian buyers. Discount code SHAWTOWIN; buy via Simforge.com or the Virtual Racing Hub. His hand-picked setups pair the pedals with a Moza R5 (beginner), R9 (semi-pro) or R12 (pro) wheel — the R5 rig works on a sturdy desk — and the Virtual Racing Hub also sells rig structures.

reels.title: The best definition of discipline
reels.summary: A shirtless man in a blue-and-white striped beanie jumps into an ice-filled metal tub on a wooden deck at dusk and sits stoically, staring into the camera, while a gravelly voiceover repeats the mantra three times: 'Discipline is choosing pleasure now over pleasure later.' On-screen text calls it the best definition of discipline — 'especially on days where you don't want to' — the ice bath as a literal metaphor for choosing short-term discomfort. Reposted by @gymxsports with credit to @jordan.ferrone, the daily ice-bath creator.

reels.title: 5 Claude Code plugins for better front-end design
reels.summary: A roundup of five additions for improving front-end work in Claude Code: Taste Skill, Vercel’s Web Design Guidelines skill, a complete design system skill, 21st Dev MCP, and Playwright CLI. The central idea is to pair stronger design references and reusable components with browser-based visual checks.

reels.title: 4 GitHub repos for advanced design effects with Claude Code
reels.summary: Cindy Zhu's tutorial 'How to create Advanced Design Effects using Claude & GitHub' argues that vibe coding with Claude Code has closed the historical gap between designers creating visuals and engineers making them functional. She shares four GitHub repos to 'steal' for projects: React Three Fiber (drops the full Three.js library into a site), Liquid Glass JS (Apple-like liquid glass effect with full controls), Shader Gradient (moving gradients customizable by shape, color, and motion in React), and Liquid Logo (a chrome liquid-metal look applicable to anything). Her workflow: don't download or hand-code these yourself — point Claude Code at the repo and describe the effect you want. From the caption she adds a caution: treat a repo as reference code, not a magic asset — check the licence, maintenance, and framework first, then ask Claude Code to isolate the smallest effect you need and adapt it inside a disposable branch before merging.

reels.title: Skill of the week: Annotated Illustrations for Claude Code
reels.summary: Remy (@aiwithremy) presents his 'Skill of the week': 'Annotated Illustrations' by designer Ian, a skill for Claude Code. His premise: vibe coding makes it easy to build working apps, but the problem is you end up not understanding how they work. Run this skill after a big build and the agent explores the codebase, maps the moving parts — components like input, auth, queue, agent, store, and notify — then generates a simple hand-drawn flowchart showing what happens and in what order. He positions it as the fix for losing track of things in complex systems and useful for briefing new teammates or non-technical collaborators, and shows the illustration it produced for an onboarding flow he built. Ends with a CTA to comment 'SKILL' to receive the tool.

reels.title: Geometric-Art.com: free tool turning footage into animated line art
reels.summary: Ramshad (@aartstock) demos Geometric-Art.com, a free website for graphic and motion designers that turns uploaded images or video into abstract animated line art. The workflow: upload a photo or clip, pick effects from the side panel, and customize — the demo shows PRO settings like PORTRAIT WINDOW and SPECTRAL CURTAIN on an athletic-wear portrait, and effects reacting automatically to motion in a sunglasses video clip. You adjust size, thickness, and colors, then export the result as a high-quality image, video, or embed.

reels.title: 3 free websites every designer needs (Part 1)
reels.summary: Jameel Haider's 'Part 1: 3 Free Websites Every Designer Needs!' is a fast-paced screen-recorded walkthrough of three free design resources. First, Shapes.Gallery — 250+ free SVG shapes for hero sections and landing pages. Second, Randoma11y.com — checks color contrast against WCAG 2.1 and APCA standards, generates accessible palettes, and toggles between light and dark modes with code outputs. Third, dotmatrix.zzzzshawn.cloud — 55+ free dot-matrix loaders built with React and shadcn (examples shown: 'Neon Drift,' 'Pulse Loader,' 'Echo Ring'), with a playground that reveals the code. Ends teasing Part 2.
reels.creator_name: Jameel Haider | AI Creator | Product Designer

reels.title: Pear: AI-generated Renaissance-style site demo ('GPT-6 Astra + Higgsfield COOKED')
reels.summary: Jerry Rogers (@jerrythewebdev) screen-records a laptop scrolling through 'Pear,' an agency website ('makes you appear') composed entirely of AI-generated video in a Renaissance/classical painting style: a figure pulling back a curtain, hands grafting a pear tree sapling, pears growing on branches, a woman holding a pear, two hands splitting a pear, workers building scaffolding around a giant pear, and constellations forming over a blue sky. The on-screen overlay reads 'GPT-6 Astra + Higgsfield COOKED,' framing the clip as amazement at what GPT-6 Astra and Higgsfield can generate. The caption invites viewers to comment 'ASTRA' for the exact setup plus free 3-day access to @higgsfield.ai (#higgsfieldCreator). Comments are mixed: some praise the visuals ('Beautiful,' 'bro it's acc crazy what AI can do'), while many dispute the AI claim ('This was made way before GPT6,' 'Already existed before'), criticize scroll-heavy sites as unusable ('you never can find anything you came for,' 'looks more like a very complex ppt presentation'), and joke about token costs ('The tokens will cost my kidney').

reels.title: Top 4 UI libraries every vibe coder should know
reels.summary: kevin (@kevin.snippet) gives a fast-paced screen-recorded walkthrough of four UI libraries for vibe coders. First, Unlumen UI — animations, image effects, navigation components, and backgrounds/shaders to make websites more interactive. Second, Magic UI — beautiful components like animated lists, theme toggles, special effects (e.g. meteors), templates, and ready-to-use showcase sections. Third, Smooth UI — stylish text effects, buttons, UI components, and prebuilt blocks such as hero sections and stats blocks for building modern sites faster. Fourth, Retro UI — neo-brutalist design with a Figma UI kit of 300+ components (carousels, cards, dropdown menus) plus blocks and templates. He closes at his desk asking viewers to comment 'Libraries' for all the links. Comments are positive and utility-focused ('Superb work,' 'Clean component libraries save so much dev time'), with several link requests and mentions of shadcn MCP and awesmos.com.

reels.title: 4 websites for building 3D interactive experiences with Three.js and AI
reels.summary: Codvyn (@codvyn) presents four starting-point websites for building 3D, interactive web experiences (speaking Hindi, at a dual-monitor desk). He opens with 'Buttermax' — a yellow, fluid, game-like site — then walks through: 1/4 threeui.com, a gallery of free and paid Three.js templates like 'KAGE' and 'RASTER RUN,' noting you can copy the template prompt for an AI agent to build it; 2/4 tasteskill.dev, 'The Anti-Slop Frontend Framework for AI Agents' for clean UI components; 3/4 gsap.com, showing smooth 3D component examples; 4/4 21st.dev, another library of paid templates. His laptop shows a 'Start it. Build it. Launch it.' page alongside. He frames these as starting points for modern web design with AI tools like Claude, and asks viewers to like and comment for all four links. Comments are enthusiastic and technical: link requests, GPU performance concerns, and suggestions to add awwwards.com.

reels.title: StringTune: lightweight animation toolkit for scroll effects with Claude Code
reels.summary: Shai (@shai.hq) presents StringTune, a lightweight JavaScript animation toolkit pitched as a leaner alternative to heavy libraries like GSAP for scroll animations. His docs walkthrough shows modules including Parallax, Glide, Progress, Lerp, and Cursor Interactions, plus homepage demos like a katana scroll effect and cloud artwork. His recommended workflow: install via `npm install @fiddle-digital/string-tune`, share the StringTune documentation URL with Claude Code, tell it the interaction you want (subtle parallax, magnetic buttons, smooth scroll reveals), and let Claude wire it into the site — he shows the animated result on a landing page. He also promotes his '100 days to become a Design Engineer with Claude Code' program (Nov 2 – Dec 6, 2026) and asks viewers to comment 'Super' for the link. Comments are mixed and technical: one viewer is confused about the difference between 'claude design' and Claude Code, another wants complex app examples beyond marketing sites (e.g. Jira-style flows), to which the creator notes he also covers fintech and healthcare apps with complex flows.
